q: 单数据中心服务全球用户会先撞到哪些瓶颈？
q_en: What bottlenecks appear when one data center serves global users?
options: 跨地域传播和排队延迟上升
源站重复向每个用户发送大对象
单点故障会拖垮整体可用性
边缘节点天然无法缓存静态内容
options_en: Long-distance propagation and queueing latency rise.
The origin repeatedly sends large objects to each user.
A single failure point can take down the whole service.
Edge nodes naturally cannot cache static content.
why: 我会先说距离、带宽和单点风险。CDN 的价值就是把热门内容和请求处理移到离用户更近的位置。
why_en: The core problems are distance, repeated origin bandwidth, and a single failure domain, which a CDN reduces by moving delivery closer to users.
optionExplanations: 光速和排队延迟不可能靠优化代码消掉，用户离数据中心越远，请求排队和往返时间就越长。
源站每次都要为每个用户重新传输同一份大文件，出口带宽和成本随用户数线性增长。
只有一个数据中心意味着它一挂，全球用户都拿不到服务，没有地理冗余。
这其实是误解——边缘节点本身完全能缓存静态内容，这正是 CDN 起作用的机制，不是它的局限。
optionExplanations_en: Speed of light and queueing delay can't be optimized away in code — the farther a user is from the data center, the longer requests queue and round-trip.
The origin re-sends the same large object to every user from scratch, so egress bandwidth and cost scale linearly with users.
A single data center means one outage takes down every global user — there's no geographic redundancy.
This is actually a misconception — edge nodes can absolutely cache static content; that's the core mechanism a CDN relies on, not a limitation.

q: 估算跨地域请求延迟时要拆成哪些部分？
q_en: Which parts should you separate when estimating cross-region request latency?
options: 信号传播时间
链路拥塞导致的排队
数据传输时间
服务端处理时间
DNS 名字长度
options_en: Signal propagation time.
Queueing from congestion.
Time to transmit bytes over the link.
Server-side processing time.
The length of the DNS name.
why: 跨洲 RTT 先受物理距离限制，再叠加排队、传输和处理。名字长度不是系统设计里的主延迟项。
why_en: Cross-region latency comes from propagation, queueing, transmission, and processing, while DNS name length is not the main design lever.

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求往返一次的网络时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RTT is the network time for a request to go out and the response to come back.

optionExplanations: 光在光纤里跑得再快也要花时间，这是任何优化都绕不开的物理下限。
链路拥塞时数据包要排队等发送，流量越大排队越久，这一项会随负载显著波动。
对象越大，把字节推上线路所需的时间就越长，这部分和带宽直接相关。
服务端要解析请求、查数据、生成响应，这段计算和 I/O 时间也算进总延迟。
这是误解——DNS 名字长短几乎不影响解析或传输耗时，不该算进延迟预算。
optionExplanations_en: Light in fiber still takes real time to travel — it's a physical floor no optimization removes.
When a link is congested, packets sit in a queue before they're sent, so this term swings a lot with load.
Bigger objects take longer to push onto the wire, so this term scales with payload size and bandwidth.
The server has to parse the request, hit storage, and build a response — that compute and I/O time counts too.
This is a misconception — DNS name length barely affects resolution or transfer time and shouldn't be in the latency budget.

scenario: 一个视频站点的源站在美国东部，欧洲用户反复请求同一批热门视频片段。
scenario_en: A video site has its origin in the eastern US, while European users repeatedly request the same hot video segments.
q: CDN 的核心结构是什么？
q_en: What is the core structure of a CDN?
options: 把所有用户请求强制回源
在多个地理位置放代理缓存
只给源站增加更大的数据库
让客户端互相转发内容
options_en: Force every user request back to the origin.
Place proxy caches across geographic locations.
Only add a larger database at the origin.
Let clients relay content to each other.
why: CDN 是一组靠近用户的代理缓存，命中时直接从边缘返回。这样少走长距离网络，也少压源站出口带宽。
why_en: A CDN is a set of geographically distributed edge proxies that serve cached content near users and reduce origin bandwidth.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    U["User"] --> E["Nearby edge proxy"]
    E -->|cache hit| U
    E -->|miss| O["Origin"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 把内容缓存在多个边缘位置的分发网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN is a delivery network that caches content at multiple edge locations.

optionExplanations: 这恰恰是 CDN 想避免的——每次都回源等于放弃了缓存带来的所有好处。
核心结构就是把代理缓存分布到多个地理位置，命中时在边缘直接应答，不必每次绕回源站。
只扩容源站数据库解决不了距离问题，用户到源站的物理距离和跳数完全没变。
客户端互相转发涉及信任和一致性风险，真正起作用的是运营方管理的边缘代理，不是点对点转发。
optionExplanations_en: That's exactly what a CDN avoids — always going back to origin throws away every benefit caching gives you.
The core structure is proxy caches spread across many geographic locations, answering directly at the edge on a hit instead of routing back to origin every time.
Just adding origin database capacity doesn't fix distance — the physical hops between the user and origin stay the same.
Peer-to-peer client relaying raises trust and consistency risks; the real mechanism is operator-managed edge proxies, not clients forwarding to each other.

scenario: 一个 Web 应用既有数据库热点读，也有全球用户下载静态图片的延迟问题。
scenario_en: A web app has hot database reads and also global latency for downloading static images.
q: 区分普通缓存和 CDN 时看哪条轴？
q_en: What axis separates a regular cache from a CDN?
options: 是否一定使用 SQL
是否跨地域把内容放到网络边缘
是否只能缓存动态内容
是否必须由浏览器实现
options_en: Whether it must use SQL.
Whether content is distributed to network edges across regions.
Whether it can cache only dynamic content.
Whether it must be implemented by the browser.
why: 普通缓存主要缩短应用到后端的路径，CDN 主要缩短终端用户到内容的网络路径。两者都能降延迟，但作用位置不同。
why_en: A normal cache shortens the app-to-backend path, while a CDN shortens the user-to-content network path.
tradeoff: 应用后端负载 vs 全球网络距离

termDefinitions.meaning: 把内容缓存在多个边缘位置的分发网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content at edge locations close to users.

optionExplanations: SQL 与否是存储技术选型，跟缓存放在哪一层完全无关，不是区分普通缓存和 CDN 的轴。
关键轴是内容有没有跨地域推到网络边缘——这决定了缩短的是应用到后端的路径，还是用户到内容的路径。
普通缓存和 CDN 都能缓存动态内容片段，「只能缓存动态」这个限定本身就不成立。
缓存不必由浏览器实现，服务端、代理和边缘节点都能承担缓存角色。
optionExplanations_en: Whether you use SQL is a storage choice, unrelated to which layer caching sits in — it's not the axis that separates ordinary caching from a CDN.
The real axis is whether content moves across regions to the network edge, deciding if you're shortening the app-to-backend path or the user-to-content path.
Both ordinary caching and CDNs can cache dynamic fragments, so the premise that either 'can only cache dynamic content' is false.
Caching doesn't require a browser implementation — servers, proxies, and edge nodes can all hold the cache role.

scenario: 媒体公司要分发版本稳定的大电影文件，发布时间可控，目标是上线后边缘节点立刻有副本。
scenario_en: A media company distributes stable movie files with controlled release times, and edge nodes should already have copies at launch.
q: 该优先选 Push CDN 还是 Pull CDN？
q_en: Should this use a push CDN or a pull CDN first?
options: Push CDN：源站提前把对象送到边缘
Pull CDN：第一次用户请求时再回源
只用浏览器缓存
只把数据库复制到边缘
options_en: Push CDN: the origin sends objects to edges ahead of time.
Pull CDN: edges fetch from origin on the first user request.
Use only browser caching.
Replicate only the database to the edge.
why: 我会选 Push，因为内容稳定且发布时间可控，提前铺到边缘能避免首批用户同时回源。代价是存储更多副本，内容频繁变更时会浪费推送。
why_en: I would choose push because stable scheduled content can be preloaded at the edge before user traffic arrives.
whenOtherWins: 如果对象很多、访问长尾明显或内容变化快，Pull 能只缓存被真正访问的对象。
tradeoff: 预热可用性 vs 存储和推送成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 把内容缓存在多个边缘位置的分发网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content at edge locations close to users.

optionExplanations: 内容版本稳定、发布时间可控时，提前把大文件推到边缘能让上线瞬间就有本地副本，不用等首批用户排队回源。
长尾对象多、访问模式不确定时更合适，只缓存真被请求过的内容能省边缘存储，但本题发布时间可控，用不上这个优势。
浏览器缓存只对单个用户的重复访问有效，帮不了其他用户的首次请求，解决不了全局预热问题。
复制数据库到边缘针对的是读写一致性问题，不是静态大文件的分发预热，用错了层。
optionExplanations_en: When the content version is stable and the release time is known ahead, pushing the large file to the edge early means a local copy exists the moment it launches, instead of the first wave of users all going back to origin.
This fits better when there are many long-tail objects and access is unpredictable — it only caches what's actually requested; but here release timing is known, so that edge doesn't help.
Browser caching only helps repeat visits from the same user — it does nothing for other users' first request, so it can't solve the pre-warming problem.
Replicating the database to the edge addresses read/write consistency, not pre-warming a static large file — that's solving the problem at the wrong layer.

scenario: 新闻站点每天产生大量页面，只有少数会爆火，且内容更新频繁。
scenario_en: A news site creates many pages per day, only a few go viral, and content changes frequently.
q: 默认更适合哪种 CDN 填充模式？
q_en: Which CDN fill model fits better by default?
options: Pull：被访问后再缓存并设置 TTL
Push：所有页面发布时全量推边缘
禁止缓存所有动态页面
只在源站前加一个 SQL 读副本
options_en: Pull: cache after access and attach a TTL.
Push: send every page to all edges at publish time.
Disable caching for every dynamic page.
Only add a SQL read replica in front of the origin.
why: 我会选 Pull，因为长尾页面很多，按需缓存能少占边缘存储。代价是首个请求会回源，所以热点页可以再做预热。
why_en: Pull fits long-tail frequently changing pages because the CDN stores only objects that users actually request.
whenOtherWins: 如果发布前就知道哪些页面一定高流量，Push 或预热清单会更好。
tradeoff: 边缘存储效率 vs 首次访问延迟

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存对象在重新校验前可以保留的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a cached object may be used before revalidation.

optionExplanations: 页面长尾多、多数只被访问几次时，按需缓存并设 TTL 能避免把边缘存储浪费在冷门页面上。
发布前就能确定哪些页面必火时更合适，能省掉首次访问回源的延迟，但本题内容更新频繁、爆款不可预知，提前全量推的意义不大。
完全禁止缓存动态页面等于放弃了 CDN 能带来的所有延迟收益，是过度保守的极端做法。
SQL 读副本解决的是数据库读压力，跟页面要不要放到离用户更近的边缘是两个不同的问题。
optionExplanations_en: With a long tail of pages that each get only a few hits, caching on demand with a TTL avoids wasting edge storage on content nobody reads.

This fits better when you already know which pages will go viral before publishing — it skips the first-request origin trip; but here content changes often and hits are unpredictable, so pre-pushing everything buys little.
Banning caching for all dynamic pages throws away every latency win a CDN offers — it's an overly conservative extreme.
A SQL read replica addresses database read load, a different problem from whether pages sit closer to users at the edge.

q: 混合 CDN 填充模式怎么用？
q_en: How should a hybrid CDN fill model be used?
text: 我会把可预测热点走 {{Push/预热}}，把长尾和变化快的对象走 {{Pull/按需拉取}}。
text_en: Use {{push or prewarming}} for predictable hot content, and use {{pull on demand}} for long-tail or frequently changing objects.
why: 混合模式把发布确定性和存储效率拆开处理。面试里可以先说默认 Pull，再给热点预热作为优化。
why_en: A hybrid model separates predictable hot objects from long-tail objects so you get prewarming without caching everything everywhere.

q: CDN 命中路径的正确顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the correct order of a CDN request path?
steps: 边缘代理命中缓存后直接返回内容
客户端通过路由/DNS 获得合适边缘节点
若启用清洗，恶意流量先被 scrubber 过滤
边缘未命中时再向父缓存或源站取对象
why: 先选边缘，再过滤风险流量，然后优先用边缘缓存。只有 miss 才进入父缓存或源站，这是保护源站的关键。
why_en: The request should be routed to an edge, optionally scrubbed, served from cache first, and only then escalated to parent cache or origin on a miss.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    C["Client"] --> R["Routing/DNS"] --> S["Scrubber"] --> E["Edge proxy"]
    E -->|hit| C
    E -->|miss| P["Parent cache"] --> O["Origin"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 把域名解析到可连接地址或解析链路的系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS maps names to reachable addresses or routing answers.

q: CDN 路由系统选择边缘节点时应看哪些信号？
q_en: What signals should CDN routing use to pick an edge node?
options: 用户到节点的网络距离
节点当前负载和健康状态
对象是否已在该节点附近
文件名是否更短
URI 命名空间归属
options_en: Network distance from the user to the node.
Current node load and health.
Whether the object is already near that node.
Whether the file name is shorter.
The URI namespace delegated to the CDN.
why: 最近不是地理距离最短，而是网络路径、容量、负载和内容位置共同决定。文件名长度不该影响边缘选择。
why_en: The nearest edge is determined by network path, capacity, load, health, and content placement, not by the length of the file name.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标识一个 Web 对象或资源的字符串。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A URI is a string that identifies a web object or resource.

optionExplanations: 网络路径近的节点通常往返时间更短，是路由决策最直接的信号之一。
节点如果超载或不健康，就算离用户近也会拖慢响应，负载和健康必须一起看。
对象已经在附近节点意味着能直接命中，不用触发一次额外的填充或回源。
这是误解——文件名字符数跟网络路径、负载或缓存状态毫无关系，不该影响路由决策。
不同 URI 命名空间可能绑定不同的内容集群，归属关系决定了该去哪组节点找对象。
optionExplanations_en: A node with a shorter network path usually means a shorter round trip — one of the most direct routing signals.
An overloaded or unhealthy node slows responses even if it's geographically close, so load and health have to be weighed together.
If the object already sits on a nearby node, that's a direct hit — no extra fill or origin trip needed.
This is a misconception — filename length has nothing to do with network path, load, or cache state, and shouldn't affect routing.
Different URI namespaces can map to different content clusters, so namespace ownership decides which group of nodes to even look in.

scenario: CDN 检测到某地区请求量异常，里面混有大量伪造流量，但正常用户仍要访问静态资源。
scenario_en: A CDN detects abnormal traffic from one region with many fake requests, while legitimate users still need static assets.
q: 应该把哪类组件放在边缘前面？
q_en: Which component should sit before the edge proxy?
options: Scrubber 清洗服务器
更大的源站数据库
浏览器本地索引
离线报表任务
options_en: Scrubber servers.
A larger origin database.
A browser-side local index.
An offline reporting job.
why: 我会让 scrubber 先分离恶意和正常流量，再把干净请求交给边缘代理。代价是多一跳，且清洗规则误判会伤正常请求。
why_en: Use scrubbers to filter malicious traffic before it reaches the edge, while accepting an extra hop and possible false positives.
whenOtherWins: 如果没有攻击迹象，直接路由到健康边缘能减少链路复杂度和延迟。
tradeoff: 攻击隔离 vs 正常路径额外延迟

termDefinitions.meaning: 大量分布式来源同时消耗服务资源的攻击。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DDoS is an attack where many distributed sources consume service resources at once.

optionExplanations: 面对混有伪造流量的异常请求量，先用清洗服务器把恶意流量和正常用户分开，再放行干净请求，能保护后面的边缘代理。
扩大源站数据库能扛更多合法查询，但对着伪造流量硬扛只会让攻击流量也一起被放大，解决不了识别问题。
浏览器本地索引只服务单个用户自己的请求，挡不住来自外部网络的攻击流量。
离线报表是事后分析用的批处理任务，无法在攻击发生时实时拦截流量。
optionExplanations_en: When traffic volume looks anomalous and mixed with forged requests, a scrubber separates malicious from legitimate traffic first, then passes clean requests on to protect the edge proxies behind it.
A bigger origin database can absorb more legitimate queries, but throwing capacity at forged traffic just scales up the attack too — it doesn't solve the identification problem.
A local browser index only serves that one user's own requests — it can't stop attack traffic coming from the wider network.
Offline reporting is a batch job for after-the-fact analysis; it can't intercept traffic in real time while an attack is happening.

scenario: 边缘节点同时保存热门图片和很少访问的长尾文件，内存容量有限。
scenario_en: An edge node stores hot images and rarely accessed long-tail files, but memory is limited.
q: 冷热内容该怎么放？
q_en: How should hot and cold content be placed?
options: 热点放 RAM，冷内容落 SSD/HDD
所有对象都只放 RAM
所有对象都每次回源
冷内容放 RAM，热点放磁盘
options_en: Put hot content in RAM and cold content on SSD/HDD.
Put every object only in RAM.
Fetch every object from origin every time.
Put cold content in RAM and hot content on disk.
why: 热点内容吃的是低延迟，RAM 能减少磁盘访问；长尾内容放 SSD/HDD 仍比跨地域回源快。代价是边缘要做淘汰和分层存储管理。
why_en: Hot content belongs in RAM for low latency, while long-tail content can sit on SSD or HDD and still avoid distant origin fetches.
whenOtherWins: 如果对象全集很小且成本允许，全 RAM 可以简化路径；如果内容有强隐私约束，可能不放边缘。
tradeoff: 低延迟命中 vs 边缘存储成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 速度快但容量成本高的内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RAM is fast memory with higher cost per capacity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 比机械磁盘快、比内存便宜的持久存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SSD is persistent storage faster than a hard disk and cheaper than RAM per capacity.

optionExplanations: 内存容量有限时，把访问频繁的内容放 RAM 吃低延迟，长尾内容落盘，仍比每次跨地域回源快得多。
如果对象总量本身很小、成本允许，全放 RAM 能省掉分层管理，但本题内存容量有限，装不下全部内容。
每次都回源等于放弃了边缘缓存的全部价值，命中率会退化到接近零。
这个顺序刚好反了——冷内容访问少，占着内存反而挤掉真正该低延迟的热点内容。
optionExplanations_en: With limited memory, keeping frequently accessed content in RAM gets low latency, while long-tail content spills to disk — still far faster than going back to origin every time.
If the total object set is small and cost allows, keeping everything in RAM skips tiering management; but here memory is limited and can't hold everything.
Sending every request back to origin throws away all the value of edge caching — the hit rate would collapse to near zero.
This ordering is backwards — cold content is rarely accessed, so parking it in memory just crowds out the hot content that actually needs low latency.

scenario: 一个新热点视频突然在全球爆火，若每个边缘 miss 都直接回源，源站出口会被打满。
scenario_en: A new hot video goes viral globally; if every edge miss goes directly to origin, origin egress will saturate.
q: 最该加哪种 CDN 结构保护源站？
q_en: Which CDN structure best protects the origin?
options: 父/子多级缓存
所有边缘同时回源
客户端轮询源站健康
把源站数据库改成强一致
options_en: Parent-child hierarchical caches.
Let all edges fetch from origin at once.
Have clients poll origin health.
Make the origin database strongly consistent.
why: 我会让边缘先找父缓存，父缓存再少量回源。这样把 N 个边缘 miss 合并成更少的源站请求，但层级会增加一次内部跳转。
why_en: Hierarchical caches let edges fetch from parents first, collapsing many edge misses into fewer origin requests.
whenOtherWins: 如果 CDN 规模很小、对象很少，单层边缘可能够用，层级缓存反而增加运维。
tradeoff: 源站出口保护 vs 层级路径复杂度
diagram:
flowchart BT
    O["Origin"] --> P1["Parent cache"]
    O --> P2["Parent cache"]
    P1 --> E1["Edge A"]
    P1 --> E2["Edge B"]
    P2 --> E3["Edge C"]
optionExplanations: 热点视频全球爆火时，让边缘先找父缓存、父缓存再少量回源，能把大量并发 miss 合并成极少的源站请求。
所有边缘同时回源正是要避免的场景——瞬间并发直接打满源站出口，这就是这道题在防的问题。
客户端轮询只能发现源站是否健康，挡不住大量并发请求同时涌向源站的问题。
强一致解决的是数据正确性问题，跟源站出口带宽被打满是两码事，改一致性模型没用。
optionExplanations_en: When a hot video suddenly goes viral worldwide, letting edges check a parent cache first — with the parent making only a few origin requests — collapses a flood of concurrent misses into a tiny number of origin hits.
Every edge hitting origin at once is exactly the failure mode this needs to avoid — a burst of concurrent misses would saturate origin egress instantly.
Client polling only tells you whether origin is healthy — it does nothing to stop a flood of concurrent requests from hitting origin at once.
Strong consistency addresses data correctness, a separate problem from origin egress being saturated; changing the consistency model doesn't help here.

scenario: 边缘代理已有对象 v3，向源站请求时带上当前版本号。
scenario_en: An edge proxy already has object version v3 and sends that current version when asking the origin.
q: Retrieve API 带版本号的价值是什么？
q_en: Why should a retrieve API include the current content version?
options: 源站可只在版本变化时返回新内容
客户端可以跳过 TLS
DNS 可以永久不更新
边缘可以删除所有缓存
options_en: The origin can return new content only when the version changed.
Clients can skip TLS.
DNS never needs to update.
The edge can delete all cached content.
why: 版本号让回源请求变成条件校验：没变就复用缓存，变了再取新对象。代价是每个对象要维护可比较的版本元数据。
why_en: A version parameter turns origin fetch into revalidation, so unchanged objects do not need to be transferred again.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统之间约定好的调用接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API is a defined interface that systems use to call each other.

optionExplanations: 带上版本号让回源变成一次条件检查——没变就直接复用现有缓存，省掉重复传输整个对象。
版本号是内容一致性机制，跟传输层加不加密完全无关，不能替代 TLS。
版本号帮的是内容校验，不涉及域名解析，DNS 记录该更新还是要更新。
版本号的作用恰恰是决定哪些缓存该保留、哪些该刷新，不是无差别删光。
optionExplanations_en: Attaching a version number turns the origin request into a conditional check — if nothing changed, the edge just reuses its existing copy instead of re-transferring the whole object.
The version number is a content-consistency mechanism, unrelated to the transport layer — it can't substitute for TLS.
The version number helps content validation, not name resolution — DNS records still need to be updated on their own schedule.
The whole point of the version number is deciding which cached copies to keep and which to refresh, not deleting everything indiscriminately.

scenario: 同一个 PoP 内有多个代理，某个边缘 miss，但附近代理可能已经有该对象。
scenario_en: A PoP has several proxies; one edge misses, but a nearby peer may already have the object.
q: 回源前应先尝试什么？
q_en: What should the edge try before going to origin?
options: 在同 PoP peers 或共享索引里查找
立即让客户端直接重试连接源站服务器
把这个对象的 TTL 直接设成永不刷新
把所有同类对象从边缘节点全部清除
options_en: Check same-PoP peers or a shared index first.
Immediately have the client retry connecting straight to the origin server.
Set this object's TTL to never refresh at all.
Purge every similar object from the edge nodes entirely.
why: 同 PoP 查询通常比跨地域回源便宜，能提高命中率并保护源站。代价是广播或共享索引也要控制开销。
why_en: Searching local peers is cheaper than a distant origin fetch and can raise the hit rate without overloading the origin.
whenOtherWins: 如果对象权限敏感或 peer 查询成本高于回源，直接回源更可控。
tradeoff: 局部复用命中率 vs peer 查询开销

termDefinitions.meaning: CDN 在某个网络位置部署的一组边缘节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A PoP is a group of CDN edge nodes deployed at a network location.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存对象在重新校验前可以保留的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a cached object may be used before revalidation.

optionExplanations: 同一个 PoP 里附近代理可能已经有这个对象，先查 peer 或共享索引比跨地域回源便宜得多。
如果对象权限敏感或 peer 查询本身很贵，直接回源反而更省事；但本题邻近代理很可能已有副本，先查更划算。
把 TTL 设成无限大解决的是刷新频率问题，跟这次 miss 该不该先查 peer 完全无关，还会带来陈旧数据风险。
删掉同类对象只会让命中率更差，跟找到已有副本的目标背道而驰。
optionExplanations_en: Another proxy in the same PoP may already hold this object, so checking peers or a shared index first is usually far cheaper than a cross-region origin trip.

When objects are permission-sensitive or peer lookups themselves are expensive, going straight to origin can be more predictable; but here a nearby proxy likely already has a copy, so checking first pays off.
Setting TTL to infinite is about refresh frequency, unrelated to whether this particular miss should check peers first, and it also risks serving stale data forever.
Deleting similar objects only makes the hit rate worse — the opposite of finding a copy that already exists.

scenario: 源站发布了图片的新版本，旧版本已经散落在多个边缘节点。
scenario_en: The origin publishes a new image version, while old copies already exist on multiple edge nodes.
q: 跨边缘失效要走哪条状态链？
q_en: What state chain should cross-edge invalidation follow?
options: 版本变更→失效→重取→新版返回
版本变更→旧版继续无限期返回
随机删对象→源站不记录版本
客户端猜测→自行选择最新副本
options_en: Version changes, invalidate, refetch, and serve the new copy.
Version changes, but old copies are served forever.
Randomly delete objects and keep no origin version.
Clients guess and choose the newest copy themselves.
why: 失效不是一句 purge 就结束，要有版本变化、边缘动作和下一次读的结果。代价是全网立即失效会放大控制面流量。
why_en: Invalidation needs a full chain from version change to edge action to the next read, and immediate global purge increases control-plane traffic.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant O as Origin
    participant C as Control
    participant E as Edge
    O->>C: publish v4 / purge v3
    C->>E: invalidate object
    E->>O: refetch on next request
    E-->>E: store v4
optionExplanations: 完整链条是版本变了先让旧副本失效，下次读触发重取，边缘再返回新版本给用户。
这个说法漏掉了失效这一步——版本变了却让旧版本无限期继续服务，用户永远读不到更新。
随机删除且不记录版本等于放弃了追踪一致性的能力，边缘不知道自己删的到底是不是过期数据。
客户端没有权威信息判断哪个副本是最新的，让它自己猜测只会导致不同用户看到不同版本。
optionExplanations_en: The full chain is: version changes, the stale copy is invalidated, the next read triggers a re-fetch, and the edge returns the new version to the user.
This skips the invalidation step entirely — if the old version keeps being served indefinitely after a change, users never see the update.
Deleting objects at random with no version bookkeeping means the edge has no way to know whether what it removed was actually stale.
Clients have no authoritative way to know which copy is newest — letting them guess just means different users end up seeing different versions.

scenario: 天气页面大部分 HTML 可缓存，只有城市、时间和第三方天气片段需要动态生成。
scenario_en: A weather page is mostly cacheable HTML, but city, time, and third-party weather fragments must be dynamic.
q: 哪种边缘优化最合适？
q_en: Which edge optimization fits best?
options: 边缘脚本在代理上组装动态片段
每次都回源生成整页
把所有天气数据写进客户端 cookie
关闭 CDN
options_en: Run edge scripts to assemble dynamic fragments on the proxy.
Generate the whole page at origin every time.
Store all weather data in client cookies.
Turn off the CDN.
why: 我会把轻量参数化逻辑放到边缘，静态部分继续缓存。代价是边缘运行环境要受限，复杂业务逻辑仍应留在源站。
why_en: Edge scripting keeps static parts cached while generating lightweight dynamic fragments near the user.
whenOtherWins: 如果动态逻辑依赖强一致交易数据，回源生成更安全。
tradeoff: 边缘低延迟组装 vs 源站业务控制
optionExplanations: 大部分 HTML 可缓存、只有少数片段要动态生成时，让边缘脚本在代理上组装这些轻量片段，静态部分继续走缓存。
如果动态逻辑依赖强一致的交易数据，每次回源生成整页会更安全；但天气片段这种轻量数据没必要这么重。
把全部数据塞进客户端 cookie 会让请求体积膨胀，还会把展示逻辑暴露给客户端，管理成本更高。
关闭 CDN 会让所有原本能缓存的静态 HTML 也失去边缘加速，代价远大于只做局部动态组装。
optionExplanations_en: When most of the HTML is cacheable and only a few fragments need dynamic generation, running edge scripts on the proxy to assemble just those lightweight fragments keeps the static part cached.
If the dynamic logic depended on strongly consistent transactional data, regenerating the whole page from origin every time would be safer; but lightweight weather fragments don't need that weight.
Stuffing all the data into a client cookie bloats every request and exposes rendering logic to the client, which is harder to manage.
Turning off the CDN loses edge acceleration for all the static HTML that was cacheable too — a much bigger cost than just handling the dynamic fragments locally.

scenario: 商品页的主体和图片能缓存，库存和价格片段必须从源站校验。
scenario_en: A product page has cacheable body and images, but inventory and price fragments must be checked at the origin.
q: 应考虑哪种页面组装机制？
q_en: Which page assembly mechanism should be considered?
options: ESI：边缘组合缓存片段和动态片段
Anycast：所有片段共享一个 IP
BGP leak：让路由绕远
只靠磁盘扩容源站
options_en: ESI: the edge combines cached fragments with dynamic fragments.
Anycast: all fragments share one IP.
BGP leak: route traffic through unintended paths.
Only expand origin disks.
why: ESI 适合整页不该全量回源、但少数片段要动态刷新的页面。代价是页面模板和缓存边界要设计清楚。
why_en: ESI fits pages where most fragments are cacheable but a few fragments must be fetched or refreshed dynamically.
whenOtherWins: 如果页面每个部分都高度个性化，服务端渲染或应用层缓存更直接。
tradeoff: 片段级缓存 vs 模板复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: 在边缘把缓存片段和动态片段组合成响应的标记机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ESI is a markup mechanism for assembling cached and dynamic fragments at the edge.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络层地址和转发协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP is the network-layer addressing and forwarding protocol.

optionExplanations: 商品主体和图片能缓存、只有库存价格要校验时，ESI 让边缘按模板把缓存片段和动态片段拼成一整页。
Anycast 解决的是网络路由问题，不是页面内不同片段该怎么组装，用错了层。
BGP leak 是一种路由故障，不是页面组装机制，跟这道题要解决的问题无关。
只扩磁盘解决不了缓存边界问题，库存价格该多久校验一次的判断根本不在存储层。
optionExplanations_en: When the product body and images are cacheable but stock and price must be verified live, ESI lets the edge assemble cached fragments and dynamic fragments into one page from a template.
Anycast solves network routing, not how different fragments inside a page get assembled — that's the wrong layer for this problem.
A BGP leak is a routing failure mode, not a page-assembly mechanism, and it's unrelated to what this question is asking.
Adding origin disk capacity doesn't touch the caching-boundary question at all — deciding how often stock and price get revalidated isn't a storage-layer decision.

q: DASH 为什么适合 CDN 上的视频分发？
q_en: Why does DASH fit video delivery over a CDN?
text: DASH 用一个 {{manifest/清单}} 指向多种码率片段，客户端按网络状况选择 {{分辨率/码率}}。
text_en: DASH uses a {{manifest}} that points to segments at multiple bitrates, and the client chooses the {{resolution or bitrate}} based on network conditions.
why: CDN 只需要分发可缓存的视频片段，质量选择留给客户端。这样弱网用户降码率，高带宽用户拿更清晰版本。
why_en: DASH lets the CDN cache video segments while the client adapts bitrate to current network conditions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通过 HTTP 分发多码率视频片段的自适应流媒体方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DASH is adaptive video streaming over HTTP using segments at multiple bitrates.

scenario: 你要把 `static.example.com` 交给 CDN，并希望故障或拥塞时能较快把用户切到其他 PoP。
scenario_en: You delegate `static.example.com` to a CDN and want users shifted to another PoP quickly during failure or congestion.
q: 哪种路由方式最常用来做这件事？
q_en: Which routing method is commonly used for this?
options: DNS 重定向配短 TTL
客户端随机挑服务器
源站永远返回同一 IP
把所有对象嵌进 HTML
options_en: DNS redirection with a short TTL.
Let the client randomly choose a server.
Have the origin always return one IP.
Embed every object into HTML.
why: DNS 路由能把用户映射到合适网络位置，再在 PoP 内做负载均衡。短 TTL 让故障切换更快，但会增加解析请求量。
why_en: DNS redirection maps users to a suitable PoP and short TTLs allow faster traffic shifts during failures.
whenOtherWins: 如果只追求极简接入，小站可以用 HTTP 302；如果网络层已有成熟 Anycast，也可用共享 IP 接入。
tradeoff: 路由控制灵活性 vs DNS 解析开销

termDefinitions.meaning: 把域名解析到地址或 CDN 路由答案的系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS maps domain names to addresses or CDN routing answers.

termDefinitions.meaning: DNS 或缓存答案在重新获取前可保留的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a DNS or cache answer can be reused before refresh.

termDefinitions.meaning: CDN 在某个网络位置部署的一组边缘节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A PoP is a CDN deployment at a network location.

optionExplanations: 要在故障或拥塞时较快把用户切到别的 PoP，DNS 重定向配短 TTL 能让解析结果更快跟上变化。
客户端没有全局负载和网络状况的信息，随机挑选可能恰好选中拥塞或故障的节点。
源站固定返回同一 IP 意味着没有任何调度空间，一旦那个节点出问题所有用户都受影响。
把对象嵌进 HTML 是内容组织方式，跟怎么把用户路由到合适的服务器毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: To move users to another PoP quickly during a failure or congestion, DNS redirection with a short TTL lets resolution results catch up with changes faster.
Clients have no visibility into global load or network conditions, so picking randomly can easily land on a congested or failing node.
Origin always returning the same IP leaves zero room to steer traffic — if that one node has a problem, every user is affected.
Embedding objects in HTML is a content-organization choice, unrelated to how users get routed to the right server.

scenario: CDN 团队在比较 Anycast 和 DNS 路由，目标都是把用户送到可用边缘。
scenario_en: A CDN team compares Anycast and DNS routing; both aim to send users to a usable edge.
q: Anycast 和 DNS 路由的关键差异是什么？
q_en: What is the key difference between Anycast and DNS routing?
options: Anycast 依赖 BGP 路径，DNS 路由由解析答案控制
Anycast 只能服务数据库，DNS 只能服务图片
Anycast 不需要任何网络路由
DNS 路由不能考虑负载
options_en: Anycast relies on BGP paths, while DNS routing controls the resolver answer.
Anycast only serves databases and DNS only serves images.
Anycast needs no network routing.
DNS routing cannot consider load.
why: Anycast 是同一 IP 在多地宣告，让网络自然选路径；DNS 是解析时返回不同目标。取舍是网络层自动性和应用层调度控制。
why_en: Anycast advertises one IP from many places and lets routing pick a path, while DNS routing changes the answer returned to clients.
tradeoff: 网络层自动路由 vs 解析层显式调度

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个地点宣告同一个 IP，由网络路由把用户带到某个近端地点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Anycast advertises the same IP from multiple locations and routing sends users to a nearby site.

termDefinitions.meaning: 互联网自治系统之间交换路由的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BGP is the routing protocol used between Internet autonomous systems.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把域名解析到地址或路由答案的系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS maps domain names to addresses or routing answers.

optionExplanations: 对，Anycast 靠同一 IP 多地宣告，网络层通过 BGP 自动选路径；DNS 路由则是应用层直接决定返回哪个目标。
这两种路由方式跟内容类型（数据库还是图片）没有关系，都是通用的流量调度机制。
Anycast 恰恰依赖网络路由——它靠的就是 BGP 帮忙自动挑最短路径，不是不需要路由。
DNS 路由完全可以在解析层结合健康和负载信息决定返回哪个目标，不是天生瞎选。
optionExplanations_en: Right — Anycast announces the same IP from many locations and lets the network layer pick a path via BGP, while DNS routing decides which target to return at the application layer.
These two routing approaches have nothing to do with content type (database vs. images) — both are general-purpose traffic-steering mechanisms.
Anycast actually depends on network routing — it relies on BGP to automatically pick the shortest path, it isn't routing-free.
DNS routing absolutely can factor in health and load at resolution time to decide which target to return — it isn't inherently blind.

scenario: 小站点先不接复杂 CDN DNS，只想让浏览器从源站跳到静态资源域名。
scenario_en: A small site does not want complex CDN DNS yet and only needs the browser to jump from origin to a static asset domain.
q: HTTP 重定向的真实响应长什么样？
q_en: What does a real HTTP redirect response look like?
options: 返回 302 和 Location 头
返回 500 并让客户端重试
返回空 DNS 记录
返回数据库复制日志
options_en: Return 302 with a Location header.
Return 500 and ask the client to retry.
Return an empty DNS record.
Return database replication logs.
why: HTTP 302 是最简单的 CDN 接入方式：客户端先到源站，再按 Location 去 CDN 域名。代价是多一次往返，且源站仍在首跳路径上。
why_en: HTTP 302 is a simple CDN handoff because the browser follows the Location header to the CDN URL.
codeSample:
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Location: https://static-cdn.example.com/a.png
Cache-Control: max-age=60

termDefinitions.meaning: Web 客户端和服务器交换请求/响应的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the request-response protocol used by web clients and servers.

optionExplanations: 真实响应是 302 加一个 Location 头，浏览器读到后自动跳去 CDN 域名。
500 表示服务出错，这里源站是主动引导跳转，不是发生了错误。
重定向发生在 HTTP 响应层，跟 DNS 记录是否为空没有关系。
数据库复制日志属于存储内部状态，跟浏览器该跳去哪个域名完全是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: The real response is a 302 with a Location header — the browser reads it and automatically follows the redirect to the CDN domain.
A 500 means the service errored; here origin is deliberately steering the client to redirect, not failing.
The redirect happens at the HTTP response layer — it has nothing to do with whether a DNS record is empty.
Database replication logs are internal storage state, unrelated to which domain the browser should jump to.

scenario: CDN 把一串候选边缘地址交给客户端，让客户端自己挑一个。
scenario_en: A CDN gives the client a list of candidate edge addresses and lets the client choose one.
q: 这种 client multiplexing 最大风险是什么？
q_en: What is the main risk of client multiplexing?
options: 客户端看不到全局负载，可能选到拥塞节点
源站无法存储任何内容
所有边缘必须使用同一磁盘
浏览器不能发 HTTP 请求
options_en: The client lacks global load visibility and may pick a congested node.
The origin cannot store any content.
All edges must use the same disk.
Browsers cannot send HTTP requests.
why: 客户端能测自己到节点的局部体验，但不知道节点整体负载和缓存状态。结果可能所有客户端都冲向同一个看似近的节点。
why_en: The client can see local reachability but not global load or cache state, so it may choose a bad edge.
optionExplanations: 客户端只能测到自己这一端的体验，完全看不到节点当前的整体负载，容易一窝蜂挑中同一个看似近但已拥塞的节点。
这个风险跟源站存储能力没有关系，源站该怎么存内容没有因为客户端选边缘而受限。
边缘各自用什么磁盘是内部实现细节，跟客户端自选服务器带来的风险无关。
客户端 multiplexing 本身依赖浏览器能发 HTTP 请求，这个前提并没有被打破。
optionExplanations_en: A client can only measure its own local experience — it has no view of a node's overall load, so many clients can pile onto the same seemingly-close node that's actually congested.
This risk has nothing to do with origin's storage capability — origin's ability to store content isn't constrained by clients picking their own edge.
What disk each edge uses internally is an implementation detail, unrelated to the risk created by clients choosing their own server.
Client-side multiplexing relies on the browser being able to send HTTP requests in the first place — that assumption isn't broken here.

scenario: 边缘内容可能变旧；对象大多不频繁变化，但不能无限期服务旧版本。
scenario_en: Edge content can become stale; objects usually do not change often, but old versions cannot be served forever.
q: TTL 和固定 TTR 里该先选哪个？
q_en: Should TTL or fixed TTR be the default?
options: TTL：过期后再向源站校验
固定 TTR：每隔固定时间全量刷新
永远不校验
每次请求都删缓存
options_en: TTL: revalidate with origin after expiration.
Fixed TTR: refresh on a fixed interval.
Never revalidate.
Delete the cache on every request.
why: TTL 能让未过期对象直接服务，过期后再校验是否变化。相比固定轮询，它少做无意义刷新，但仍允许短暂旧数据。
why_en: TTL avoids unnecessary refreshes by serving objects until expiration and revalidating only when needed.
whenOtherWins: 如果源站要求边缘按固定节奏同步审计数据，固定 TTR 更容易证明行为。
tradeoff: 刷新带宽 vs 可接受陈旧窗口

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存对象在重新校验前可以使用的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a cached object may be served before revalidation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存按固定周期主动刷新内容的间隔。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTR is the interval for proactively refreshing cached content.

optionExplanations: 多数对象不常变但也不能无限旧，用 TTL 让代理在有效期内直接服务，只在到期后才回源校验是否真的变了。
如果源站要求按固定节奏证明同步行为（比如审计场景），固定 TTR 更容易证明；但本题只是想少做无意义刷新，TTL 更合适。
永远不校验意味着内容一旦变了，边缘会无限期地一直返回旧版本，陈旧窗口没有上限。
每次请求都删缓存等于放弃了缓存本身，命中率会跌到零，完全违背了要控制陈旧但仍想省流量的目标。
optionExplanations_en: Most objects don't change often but still shouldn't be served stale forever, so a TTL lets the proxy serve directly while it's still valid and only checks origin once it lapses.
When origin needs proof of syncing on a fixed cadence, like an audit scenario, a fixed TTR is easier to demonstrate; but here the goal is just cutting pointless refreshes, so TTL fits better.
Never revalidating means once content changes, the edge keeps returning the old version indefinitely — there's no cap on how stale it gets.
Deleting the cache on every request throws away caching entirely — hit rate drops to zero, defeating the goal of bounding staleness while still saving bandwidth.

scenario: 源站希望减少边缘反复轮询，同时在内容变化时能通知持有副本的代理。
scenario_en: The origin wants less repeated polling from edges, while still notifying proxies that hold copies when content changes.
q: 哪种一致性机制更贴合？
q_en: Which consistency mechanism fits best?
options: Lease：源站承诺租期内变更会通知代理
固定 TTR：代理不断按周期抓取
完全禁用缓存
客户端投票决定版本
options_en: Lease: the origin promises to notify the proxy of changes during the lease.
Fixed TTR: the proxy keeps fetching on a schedule.
Disable caching entirely.
Clients vote on the version.
why: Lease 把轮询改成租约期内的变更通知，消息量通常更低。代价是源站要追踪哪些代理持有租约，并处理租约过期。
why_en: Leases reduce polling by letting the origin notify leased proxies when content changes during the lease window.
whenOtherWins: 如果源站不想维护持有者状态，短 TTL 更简单。
tradeoff: 少轮询消息 vs 源站持有者状态
optionExplanations: 源站想减少无意义轮询、又想在变更时主动通知代理，lease 让源站承诺租期内有变化会推送通知，而不是靠代理反复来问。
如果源站不想维护每个代理的持有者状态，固定 TTR 或短 TTL 更简单；但本题源站明确想主动通知，lease 更贴合。
完全禁用缓存等于放弃了所有降负载和降延迟的收益，跟一致性机制的选择完全是两个问题。
客户端没有权威信息判断哪个版本正确，让它投票只会导致不同用户看到不一致的内容。
optionExplanations_en: Origin wants to cut pointless polling while still proactively notifying proxies on change, so a lease lets origin commit to pushing a notice if anything changes during the lease period, instead of proxies repeatedly asking.
If origin doesn't want to track per-proxy holder state, a fixed TTR or short TTL is simpler; but here origin explicitly wants to notify proactively, which fits a lease better.
Disabling caching entirely throws away every load- and latency-reduction benefit, and it's a completely separate question from picking a consistency mechanism.
Clients have no authoritative way to know which version is correct, so letting them vote just leads to different users seeing inconsistent content.

q: 自适应 lease 在 CDN 里调什么？
q_en: What does an adaptive lease tune in a CDN?
text: 自适应 lease 会根据代理负载或对象热度调整 {{租约时长}}，在 {{通知状态成本}} 和 {{陈旧风险}} 之间取舍。
text_en: An adaptive lease adjusts the {{lease duration}} based on proxy load or object popularity, trading off {{notification-state cost}} against {{staleness risk}}.
why: 租约太短会频繁续约，太长会让源站维护更多通知承诺。自适应的目标是让热对象和忙节点别用同一把尺。
why_en: Adaptive leasing avoids using one fixed lease duration for all objects and loads.

scenario: CDN 要决定把代理放在 IXP 附近，还是直接放进用户 ISP 网络。
scenario_en: A CDN must decide whether to place proxies near IXPs or directly inside user ISP networks.
q: 这两个部署位置的主要取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the main tradeoff between these placements?
options: IXP 覆盖集中，ISP 更贴近最后一跳
IXP 只能存数据库，ISP 只能跑 DNS
ISP 内部署不需要任何运营合作
IXP 部署会让内容无法缓存
options_en: IXP placement is centralized; ISP placement is closer to the last mile.
IXPs only store databases and ISPs only run DNS.
ISP deployment needs no operator cooperation.
IXP placement makes caching impossible.
why: IXP 附近更容易覆盖多个网络，ISP 内部能把内容放到离用户更近的一跳。取舍是部署合作成本和最后一跳性能。
why_en: IXP sites cover many networks more centrally, while ISP sites put content closer to users at the cost of deeper operator coordination.
tradeoff: 部署覆盖效率 vs 最后一跳延迟

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个网络互联交换流量的地点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An IXP is a location where networks interconnect and exchange traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 向用户提供互联网接入的网络运营商。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ISP is a network operator that provides Internet access to users.

optionExplanations: 对，IXP 附近一个点就能覆盖多个互联网络，ISP 内部署则直接贴近用户的最后一跳，取舍在覆盖效率和最后一跳延迟之间。
这两个部署位置都能服务同一类缓存内容，跟只能跑数据库还是只能跑 DNS 没有关系。
部署进 ISP 网络内部恰恰需要跟该运营商谈合作和接入，不是不需要任何协调。
IXP 部署本身就是为了放缓存代理，内容照样能缓存，只是覆盖的网络范围和 ISP 内部署不同。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a single IXP location can cover many interconnected networks at once, while deploying inside an ISP puts content right on the user's last hop; the tradeoff is coverage efficiency versus last-hop latency.
Both deployment locations can serve the same kind of cached content — it's not that one is limited to databases and the other to DNS.
Deploying inside an ISP's network specifically requires negotiating access and partnership with that operator — it's not coordination-free.
IXP deployment exists precisely to host caching proxies — content is still cacheable there; it's the network coverage that differs from an in-ISP deployment.

scenario: 用户到远端数据中心 RTT 很高，TCP 握手和慢启动拖慢下载。
scenario_en: Users have high RTT to a distant data center, and TCP handshake plus slow start slows downloads.
q: Split TCP 为什么能改善体验？
q_en: Why can split TCP improve the experience?
options: 近端终止连接，再用持久回源长连接
关闭拥塞控制，让客户端一直猛发
改成 UDP 后完全不做重传保护
永久缓存 DNS，避免所有解析请求
options_en: Terminate nearby and use persistent long backhaul connections.
Disable congestion control and let clients send aggressively.
Switch to UDP and provide no retransmission protection.
Cache DNS forever to avoid all resolution requests.
why: 近端终止能把用户侧握手和慢启动限制在低 RTT 链路上，后端链路用稳定大窗口连接。代价是边缘代理要维护连接状态。
why_en: Split TCP reduces user-facing handshake and slow-start cost by terminating nearby and using tuned persistent backhaul connections.

termDefinitions.meaning: 提供可靠、有序字节流的传输层协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a transport protocol that provides a reliable ordered byte stream.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络请求往返一次的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RTT is the time for a network message to go out and back.

optionExplanations: 边缘代理先就近终止用户连接，握手和慢启动都发生在低 RTT 链路上，再用已经建好的持久连接把数据接力送回源。
关掉拥塞控制只会让网络更拥堵、丢包更多，不是解决高 RTT 问题的办法。
去掉重传保护意味着丢包后数据直接丢失，牺牲了可靠性，跟改善体验的目标背道而驰。
DNS 缓存解决的是名字解析开销，跟 TCP 握手和慢启动在高 RTT 链路上的代价是两个不同的问题。
optionExplanations_en: The edge proxy terminates the user's connection nearby, so the handshake and slow start happen over the low-RTT hop, then a pre-established persistent connection relays the data back to origin.
Turning off congestion control just makes the network more congested with more packet loss — it doesn't address the high-RTT problem.
Dropping retransmission protection means lost packets are simply gone, sacrificing reliability, which works against the goal of improving experience.
DNS caching addresses name-resolution overhead, a different problem from the cost of TCP handshake and slow start over a high-RTT link.

scenario: 一家视频平台每月分发 PB 级内容，第三方 CDN 成本持续上升，还想定制播放器到服务器的诊断链路。
scenario_en: A video platform distributes petabytes per month, third-party CDN cost keeps rising, and it wants custom player-to-server diagnostics.
q: 何时值得考虑专用 CDN？
q_en: When is a specialized CDN worth considering?
options: 流量巨大且需要成本、控制和诊断优化
只有一个地区的小网站
团队不想运维任何网络
内容完全不可缓存
options_en: Traffic is huge and cost, control, and diagnostics need optimization.
It is a small single-region website.
The team wants no network operations.
The content is completely uncacheable.
why: 专用 CDN 的前期建设贵，但在超大规模下能换来成本、控制和定制诊断能力。小规模业务通常先买公有 CDN。
why_en: A private CDN can pay off at massive scale when cost, control, and custom diagnostics matter more than setup simplicity.
whenOtherWins: 如果流量中等、覆盖要求常规、公有 CDN 已满足 SLA，购买服务更快也更省团队成本。
tradeoff: 自建控制与长期成本 vs 初始建设和运维负担
optionExplanations: 分发流量已经是 PB 级、第三方成本持续上涨、还想定制播放器诊断链路时，专用 CDN 的前期建设成本能靠长期规模换回来。
如果只是单地区小网站，公有 CDN 已经能满足需求，更快上线也不用自己养运维团队；但本题流量规模完全不是这个量级。
自建专用 CDN 恰恰需要团队投入运维，跟不想运维网络的诉求正好相反。
如果内容完全不可缓存，无论公有还是专用 CDN 都发挥不出缓存带来的收益，这不是选专用 CDN 的理由。
optionExplanations_en: When distribution is already petabyte-scale, third-party costs keep climbing, and you want custom player-to-server diagnostics, a dedicated CDN's upfront build cost pays off at that scale over time.
For a single-region small site, a public CDN already meets the need, ships faster, and avoids maintaining an ops team; but here the traffic is nowhere near that scale.
Building a dedicated CDN specifically requires a team to operate it — the opposite of not wanting to run any network infrastructure.
If content simply can't be cached, neither a public nor a dedicated CDN can deliver caching's benefits — that's not a reason to pick a dedicated CDN.

q: Netflix 类专用 CDN 通常想获得哪些收益？
q_en: What benefits does a Netflix-style private CDN usually target?
options: 更低长期分发成本
更强路径和服务器控制
更定制的诊断能力
让所有内容每次都回源
把用户账号数据放到边缘盒子
options_en: Lower long-term delivery cost.
More control over paths and servers.
More customized diagnostics.
Make all content fetch from origin every time.
Store user account data on edge appliances.
why: 专用 CDN 适合把大规模媒体分发做成核心能力。边缘盒子通常只服务缓存内容和上报健康，不该承担用户数据源职责。
why_en: A private CDN targets cost, control, and diagnostics for huge media delivery, not moving user-account storage to edge boxes.
optionExplanations: 自建规模够大时，摊薄下来的长期分发成本通常比一直付第三方费用更低。
自己掌控路径和服务器意味着能按自身流量模式调度，不受第三方策略限制。
自建链路可以塞进自己想要的诊断埋点，排查播放问题时能拿到第三方 CDN 给不了的细节。
这是误解——每次都回源正是专用 CDN 想避免的开销，不是它追求的收益。
边缘盒子该承担的是缓存内容和上报健康状态，把用户账号这类核心数据放进去会扩大数据泄露面。
optionExplanations_en: At large enough self-built scale, the amortized long-term distribution cost usually beats paying a third party indefinitely.
Owning your own paths and servers means you can schedule around your own traffic patterns instead of being bound by a third party's policies.
A self-built pipeline can carry whatever diagnostic instrumentation you want, giving detail a third-party CDN simply doesn't expose for debugging playback issues.
This is a misconception — always going back to origin is exactly the overhead a dedicated CDN wants to avoid, not a goal it pursues.
Edge boxes are meant to hold cached content and report health, not core data like user accounts — putting that there widens the blast radius of a breach.

q: 评估 CDN 设计时哪些点直接对应非功能需求？
q_en: Which points map directly to CDN non-functional requirements?
options: 边缘 RAM 命中降低延迟
多代理和负载均衡提高可用性
加边缘节点做水平扩展
scrubber 缓解 DDoS
把所有源站日志删掉
options_en: Edge RAM hits reduce latency.
Multiple proxies and load balancing improve availability.
Adding edge nodes provides horizontal scaling.
Scrubbers mitigate DDoS.
Delete all origin logs.
why: 性能、可用性、扩展性和安全性都能从 CDN 组件直接解释。删日志会削弱排障和审计，不是评估优势。
why_en: A CDN is evaluated through latency, availability, scalability, and security, all tied to concrete edge and routing components.

termDefinitions.meaning: 大量分布式来源同时消耗服务资源的攻击。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DDoS is an attack where many distributed sources consume service resources at once.

optionExplanations: 内存命中直接省掉磁盘和长距离网络的往返，是性能这条非功能需求最直接的体现。
多代理加负载均衡意味着单点故障不会拖垮整体服务，对应的是可用性需求。
流量涨了就加边缘节点，容量能水平扩展，对应的是扩展性需求。
scrubber 分离恶意流量，保护正常请求不被攻击流量淹没，对应的是安全性需求。
这是误解——删掉源站日志只会让排障和审计更难，是在削弱可观测性，不是在增强任何非功能属性。
optionExplanations_en: A RAM hit skips the disk trip and the long-distance network round trip entirely, the most direct expression of the performance requirement.
Multiple proxies plus load balancing mean a single failure doesn't take down the whole service — that maps to the availability requirement.
Adding edge nodes as traffic grows scales capacity horizontally — that maps to the scalability requirement.
A scrubber separates malicious traffic so legitimate requests aren't drowned out by an attack — that maps to the security requirement.
This is a misconception — deleting origin logs only makes debugging and auditing harder; it weakens observability instead of strengthening any non-functional property.

scenario: 某个边缘代理宕机，但同地区还有其他健康代理。
scenario_en: One edge proxy fails, but nearby healthy proxies are still available.
q: CDN 应如何保持可用？
q_en: How should the CDN remain available?
options: 健康检查发现故障，路由和负载均衡切到健康代理
继续把所有用户流量发送到已故障的节点
等待源站工程师人工修改 HTML 页面
要求所有用户手动清空浏览器缓存
options_en: A health check detects the failure, then routing and load balancing shift traffic to a healthy proxy.
Keep sending all user traffic to the node that's already down.
Wait for an origin engineer to manually edit the HTML page.
Ask every user to manually clear their browser cache.
why: 边缘冗余只有配合健康检查和流量切换才有用。代价是检测间隔太长会扩大故障窗口，太短会增加探测流量。
why_en: Redundant edges help only when health checks and routing quickly move traffic away from failed proxies.
optionExplanations: 健康检查先发现代理宕机，路由和负载均衡再把流量实时切到同地区还健康的代理，用户几乎无感知。
继续把用户导向已经宕机的节点，正是冗余设计想要避免的失败模式，不是保持可用的办法。
等人工去改 HTML 响应太慢，故障期间用户会持续受影响，跟自动化健康检测的目标背道而驰。
浏览器缓存跟哪个边缘代理宕机没有关系，让用户清缓存解决不了服务端的故障。
optionExplanations_en: A health check detects the proxy is down, then routing and load balancing shift traffic in real time to a healthy proxy in the same region, with users barely noticing.
Keep sending users to the already-down node — that's exactly the failure mode redundancy is meant to prevent, not a way to stay available.
Waiting for a human to edit the HTML response is far too slow — users keep being affected for the whole outage, working against the goal of automated detection.
Browser caching has nothing to do with which edge proxy is down — asking users to clear their cache doesn't fix a server-side outage.

scenario: 一个视频 CDN 的边缘命中率约 95%，每 100 个对象请求里约 95 个由边缘返回。
scenario_en: A video CDN has about a 95% edge hit ratio, so roughly 95 of every 100 object requests are served at the edge.
q: 这个数字主要喂给哪个设计判断？
q_en: What design decision does this number feed?
options: 源站出口和回源容量估算
用户密码强度估算
SQL schema 命名
前端按钮颜色
options_en: Origin egress and origin-fetch capacity estimates.
User password strength estimation.
SQL schema naming.
Frontend button color.
why: 命中率公式是 edge hits / total requests；95% 命中意味着约 5% 请求还会回源。这个数用于算源站带宽、父缓存容量和故障余量。
why_en: Hit ratio equals edge hits divided by total requests, and it drives origin egress and parent-cache capacity planning.
optionExplanations: 命中率意味着剩下约 5% 的请求会穿透到源站，这个比例直接喂给源站出口带宽和回源容量的规划。
命中率跟密码强度是完全不同领域的指标，缓存效果不会影响用户认证安全。
SQL 表怎么命名是数据库设计规范问题，跟边缘命中多少请求没有任何关系。
按钮颜色属于前端视觉设计，命中率这个后端容量指标传不到那一层。
optionExplanations_en: The hit rate implies roughly the remaining 5% of requests still pass through to origin — that fraction feeds directly into planning origin egress bandwidth and pass-through capacity.
Hit rate and password strength are metrics from completely different domains — cache effectiveness doesn't affect authentication security.
How SQL tables get named is a database-design convention, unrelated to how many requests the edge serves.
Button color is a frontend visual choice — a backend capacity metric like hit rate doesn't reach that layer.

scenario: 一个上传链路由 UI、写数据库/对象存储服务、复制服务组成；复制服务故障后，备库读不到最新视频。
scenario_en: An upload path has UI, database/blob write service, and replication service; after replication fails, the backup database lacks the newest video.
q: 分布式监控首先解决什么问题？
q_en: What problem does distributed monitoring solve first?
options: 早发现级联故障和根因线索
替代所有容错设计
保证每个请求永不失败
让数据库不需要备份
options_en: Detect cascading failures early and expose root-cause clues.
Replace every fault-tolerance design.
Guarantee every request never fails.
Make databases no longer need backups.
why: 监控不是让故障消失，而是在用户影响扩大前暴露异常趋势和依赖链。没有它，跨服务问题只能靠慢速人工排查。
why_en: Monitoring does not eliminate failures; it exposes trends and dependency clues before the user impact spreads.
optionExplanations: 复制服务故障但没人立刻知道时，监控能在用户受影响扩大前，早一步暴露异常趋势和跨服务的依赖链条。
监控是在告诉你哪里坏了，不是替你把系统变得容错——重试、降级这些容错手段还是要单独设计。
监控只负责观测，不能凭空保证请求不失败，这个承诺超出了监控本身的能力范围。
监控和数据库该不该备份是两件独立的事，看到指标不代表数据就自动有了冗余副本。
optionExplanations_en: When the replication service fails and nobody notices right away, monitoring surfaces the abnormal trend and the cross-service dependency chain before the user impact grows.
Monitoring tells you what's broken, it doesn't make the system fault-tolerant for you — retries and graceful degradation still have to be designed separately.
Monitoring only observes; it can't guarantee requests never fail out of thin air — that promise is beyond what monitoring by itself can deliver.
Whether monitoring exists and whether the database gets backed up are separate concerns — seeing metrics doesn't automatically give data a redundant copy.

scenario: 服务端日志能看到 5xx 增加，但部分用户报告页面完全打不开，服务端没有对应请求。
scenario_en: Server logs show rising 5xx, but some users report the page never opens and there are no matching server requests.
q: 服务端错误和客户端侧错误怎么区分？
q_en: How do server-side and client-side errors differ?
options: 5xx 多在后端可见；到达前失败无日志
4xx 多代表请求格式或权限等客户端问题
客户端侧错误一定都会写入后端日志
服务端错误只能等待用户主动报告
options_en: 5xx is often visible in backend telemetry; pre-arrival failures leave no server log.
4xx often reflects request-format or authorization problems.
Client-side errors are always written into backend logs.
Server-side errors can only wait for user reports.
why: 5xx 多半能从服务端日志和指标里看到；请求没到达时，服务端没有观察点。取舍是内部可观测性和外部可达性要分开监控。
why_en: Server-side failures often appear in backend telemetry, while DNS or routing failures may require external client-side monitoring.
tradeoff: 内部服务健康 vs 外部可达性

termDefinitions.meaning: 把域名解析到地址或路由答案的系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS maps domain names to addresses or routing answers.

optionExplanations: 对，5xx 通常在服务端日志和指标里能看到；但请求根本没到达服务端时，服务端完全没有观测点，这才是区分点。
4xx 确实常代表客户端问题，但这道题问的是怎么区分服务端可见错误和到达前失败，不是 4xx 与 5xx 状态码分类。
这正是本题想澄清的误解——请求没到达服务端时，根本不会有对应的日志条目，客户端侧错误不一定被后端记录。
被动等用户上报太慢，主动的客户端侧监控或外部探测能更快发现到达前的失败。
optionExplanations_en: Right — 5xx errors usually show up in server logs and metrics, but when a request never reaches the server at all, there's no server-side observation point — that's the real distinguishing line.
4xx codes often do mean a client-side issue, but this question is about distinguishing server-visible errors from failures before arrival, not 4xx vs. 5xx classification.

This is exactly the misconception the question is clarifying — when a request never reaches the server, there's no corresponding log entry at all; client-side failures aren't guaranteed to be logged on the backend.
Passively waiting for user reports is too slow — proactive client-side monitoring or external probing catches pre-arrival failures much faster.

q: 基础监控指标通常从哪些层面开始收集？
q_en: Which layers are typical starting points for basic monitoring metrics?
options: CPU、内存、磁盘、swap 等 OS 资源
网络吞吐和 RTT
Web 服务和数据库指标
机架和电源事件
用户喜欢的字体
options_en: OS resources such as CPU, memory, disk, and swap.
Network throughput and RTT.
Web-service and database metrics.
Rack and power events.
The user's favorite font.
why: 监控要覆盖主机、网络、软件和硬件环境，才能解释性能和故障。字体偏好不是运行健康信号。
why_en: Useful monitoring spans host resources, network behavior, software metrics, and hardware environment signals.

termDefinitions.meaning: 执行程序指令的处理器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CPU is the processor that executes program instructions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络消息往返一次的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RTT is the time for a network message to go out and back.

optionExplanations: CPU、内存、磁盘和 swap 耗尽是最常见的主机资源瓶颈，是监控要覆盖的第一层。
网络吞吐下降或 RTT 升高会直接拖慢跨服务调用，是排查延迟问题绕不开的信号。
Web 服务和数据库层面的指标能看到应用本身的健康状况，不只是底层主机是否正常。
机架和电源事件反映的是硬件环境层面的问题，能解释一整排机器同时异常的根因。
这是误解——用户字体偏好属于产品设计话题，跟系统运行健康完全无关，不该出现在监控指标里。
optionExplanations_en: CPU, memory, disk, and swap exhaustion are the most common host resource bottlenecks — the first layer monitoring needs to cover.
Falling network throughput or rising RTT directly slows down cross-service calls, an unavoidable signal when debugging latency.
Web-service and database-level metrics reveal the application's own health, not just whether the underlying host is fine.
Rack and power events reflect hardware-environment problems and can explain why an entire row of machines goes abnormal at once.
This is a misconception — font preference is a product-design topic, completely unrelated to system health, and doesn't belong among monitoring metrics.

scenario: 监控系统能访问每台服务器的指标端点，并希望集中控制抓取频率，避免服务端主动打爆监控入口。
scenario_en: The monitoring system can reach every server's metrics endpoint and wants central control over scrape frequency to avoid overload.
q: 指标采集该优先用 Pull 还是 Push？
q_en: Should metric collection use pull or push first?
options: Pull：监控系统按频率去抓指标
Push：每台服务器主动随时上报
只靠人工 SSH 查看
只在故障后读备份
options_en: Pull: the monitoring system scrapes metrics on a schedule.
Push: each server proactively sends metrics whenever it wants.
Only inspect machines manually over SSH.
Only read backups after failures.
why: 我会选 Pull，因为抓取频率在监控侧，能防止被大量 agent 主动上报冲垮。代价是防火墙或 NAT 后的机器可能不可达。
why_en: Pull lets the monitoring system control scrape rate, which prevents agents from overwhelming ingestion.
whenOtherWins: 如果监控系统无法连入服务器，或者客户端只能向外发，Push 更合适。
tradeoff: 中心控流 vs 网络可达性
optionExplanations: 监控系统能直接访问每台服务器的指标端点时，用 Pull 让抓取频率由监控侧统一控制，不会被大量 agent 同时上报冲垮。
如果服务器在防火墙或 NAT 后面、监控连不进去，Push 让服务器主动往外发会更可靠；但本题监控系统能直接访问端点，Pull 更简单可控。
人工 SSH 查看没法规模化，几十台以上的集群靠人盯是盯不过来的。
只在故障后才读备份数据意味着故障发生时完全没有实时可见性，等于放弃了监控本该有的时效性。
optionExplanations_en: When the monitoring system can reach every server's metrics endpoint directly, Pull lets the monitoring side control scrape frequency itself, so it's never overwhelmed by a flood of agents pushing at once.

If servers sit behind a firewall or NAT that monitoring can't reach, Push — servers reporting outward on their own — is more reliable; but here monitoring can reach the endpoints directly, so Pull is simpler and more controllable.
Manual SSH checks don't scale — nobody can keep eyes on dozens or hundreds of machines by hand.
Only reading backup data after a failure means there's zero real-time visibility during the incident itself, giving up the timeliness monitoring is supposed to provide.

scenario: 团队要保存 CPU、延迟、错误率的按时间采样数据，并支持按时间范围画趋势图。
scenario_en: A team must store time-sampled CPU, latency, and error-rate data and query ranges for trend graphs.
q: 持久化指标应优先选什么存储？
q_en: Which storage should be the default for persistent metrics?
options: TSDB
只放进单进程内存
图片文件夹
用户会话 cookie
options_en: A TSDB.
Only single-process memory.
An image folder.
User session cookies.
why: 指标天然按时间追加和按时间范围查询，TSDB 针对这种访问模式优化。代价是高分辨率长期保存很贵，要配保留和降采样策略。
why_en: A TSDB fits metrics because samples are appended and queried by time range, but retention and downsampling are needed for cost.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是本地调试的短生命周期指标，进程内存或日志就够。
tradeoff: 时间范围查询效率 vs 长期存储成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 按时间顺序存储和查询样本数据的数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TSDB stores and queries samples ordered by time.

optionExplanations: 要按时间范围查询趋势图，TSDB 天生针对「按时间追加写入、按时间范围读取」这种访问模式做了优化。
只是本地调试的短生命周期指标时，单进程内存已经够用；但本题要长期保存并支持时间范围查询，内存重启就丢了。
图片文件夹是给二进制文件用的存储方式，没有按时间索引和范围查询的能力，查趋势会非常低效。
会话 cookie 存在客户端浏览器里，容量极小又跟着单个用户会话消失，装不下持久的时间序列数据。
optionExplanations_en: To query trend charts over a time range, a TSDB is purpose-built for the 'append by time, query by time range' access pattern.
For short-lived local debugging metrics, single-process memory is enough; but here the data needs long-term storage and range queries, and memory disappears on restart.
A folder of image files is a storage shape for binary blobs — it has no time-indexing or range-query capability, so querying trends would be painfully inefficient.
A session cookie lives in the client's browser, is tiny in capacity, and disappears with that one user's session — nowhere near enough to hold persistent time-series data.

scenario: OS 指标正常，但支付服务的业务失败率升高，需要知道是哪个代码路径在失败。
scenario_en: OS metrics look normal, but the payment service's business failure rate rises and the team needs the failing code path.
q: 该补哪类观测数据？
q_en: Which observability data should be added?
options: 应用代码埋点的自定义指标/日志
只看机房电源功耗
只扩大磁盘容量
只降低仪表盘刷新率
options_en: Custom application metrics or logs from code instrumentation.
Only watch data-center power draw.
Only expand disk capacity.
Only lower dashboard refresh rate.
why: OS 指标看不见业务语义，我会在关键代码路径埋点错误码、耗时和依赖结果。代价是埋点要控制开销和字段基数。
why_en: Application instrumentation adds business-level signals that OS metrics cannot see, such as error codes and dependency results.
whenOtherWins: 如果问题明确是主机资源耗尽，先看 OS 指标更快。
tradeoff: 业务可见性 vs 埋点开销和基数

termDefinitions.meaning: 管理进程、内存、磁盘和网络等资源的系统软件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An operating system manages processes, memory, disk, and network resources.

optionExplanations: OS 指标全部正常，说明瓶颈在应用逻辑层，得往关键路径里加自定义埋点，看看是哪段代码在报错或变慢。
如果问题明确是主机资源耗尽，先看电源和硬件层信号确实更快；但这里 OS 指标已经排除了这个可能。
业务失败率升高跟磁盘容量大小没有关系，扩容磁盘解决不了代码逻辑或依赖调用的问题。
降低刷新率只是减少了看数据的频率，并没有增加任何能定位业务失败的新信息。
optionExplanations_en: With OS metrics all normal, the bottleneck sits at the application-logic layer, so instrumenting the critical path is what reveals which piece of code is erroring or slowing down.
If the problem were clearly host resource exhaustion, checking power and hardware-layer signals first would indeed be faster; but here OS metrics have already ruled that out.
A rising business failure rate has nothing to do with disk capacity — adding disk space doesn't fix a code-logic or dependency-call problem.
Lowering the refresh rate just means checking the data less often — it adds no new information that would help pinpoint the business failure.

q: 告警规则由哪两部分组成？
q_en: What two parts make up an alert rule?
text: 一个告警至少包含 {{Condition/触发条件}} 和 {{Action/响应动作}}，例如 CPU > 90% 后通知值班工程师。
text_en: An alert has a {{condition}} and an {{action}}, such as CPU > 90% and paging the on-call engineer.
why: 条件决定何时认为系统越界，动作决定谁或什么系统来处理。没有动作的阈值只是报表，不是告警。
why_en: The condition decides when the system is unhealthy, and the action decides what happens next.

termDefinitions.meaning: 执行程序指令的处理器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CPU is the processor that executes program instructions.

q: 设计服务器侧监控时应覆盖哪些对象？
q_en: What should server-side monitoring cover?
options: 关键进程崩溃
CPU、内存、磁盘、网络异常
外部依赖连通性
DNS 和路由状态
只看首页点击率
options_en: Critical process crashes.
CPU, memory, disk, and network anomalies.
Connectivity to external dependencies.
DNS and routing status.
Only homepage click-through rate.
why: 服务器侧监控要覆盖进程、资源、依赖和网络路径，才能在故障链上定位。首页点击率是产品指标，不能替代健康监控。
why_en: Server-side monitoring should cover processes, resources, dependencies, and network state so failures can be localized.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把域名解析到地址或路由答案的系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS maps domain names to addresses or routing answers.

optionExplanations: 关键进程如果崩溃退出，服务基本就等于宕机，这是最直接需要覆盖的失败信号。
CPU、内存、磁盘或网络任一项异常都可能拖垮服务响应，是主机层最基础的健康信号。
服务往往依赖别的下游系统，外部依赖不通时，本机指标再正常也救不了请求。
DNS 解析失败或路由异常会让请求根本到不了这台机器，跟主机内部指标是两个不同的故障面。
这是误解——首页点击率是产品行为指标，跟这台服务器是否健康运行没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: If a critical process crashes and exits, the service is effectively down — the most direct failure signal to cover.
A spike in CPU, memory, disk, or network can each independently drag down response times — the most basic host-level health signal.
Services often depend on downstream systems; when an external dependency is unreachable, healthy local metrics can't save the request.
A DNS failure or routing problem stops requests from ever reaching this machine — a different failure surface from internal host metrics.
This is a misconception — homepage click-through rate is a product-behavior metric, unrelated to whether this server is running healthily.

scenario: 你要画一版最小可用监控系统，先支持采集、存储、查询和可视化。
scenario_en: You need to draw a minimum viable monitoring system that supports collection, storage, querying, and visualization.
q: 最小高层架构应包含什么？
q_en: What should the minimum high-level architecture include?
options: 采集器、TSDB、查询层、仪表盘
静态页、邮件列表、人工巡检
业务主库、用户画像、营销报表
CDN 边缘、图片缓存、视频转码
options_en: Collector, TSDB, query layer, and dashboard.
Static page, mailing list, and manual inspection.
Business primary database, user profiles, and marketing reports.
CDN edge, image cache, and video transcoding.
why: collector 负责取数，TSDB 存时间序列，query service 给告警和仪表盘读数据。少了任一环，监控闭环都会断。
why_en: The collector gathers data, the TSDB stores time series, and the query service feeds alerts and dashboards.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    S["Services"] --> C["Data collector"] --> T["TSDB"] --> Q["Query service"] --> D["Dashboard"]
    Q --> A["Alert manager"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 按时间顺序存储和查询样本数据的数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TSDB stores and queries samples ordered by time.

optionExplanations: 最小闭环是采集器取数、TSDB 存时间序列、查询层供告警和仪表盘读取，缺一环整个链路就断了。
人工巡检和邮件列表没有自动化采集和存储能力，规模一大就跟不上，撑不起最小可用系统的定位。
业务主库和营销报表是产品数据栈的组成部分，跟运行健康监控要解决的问题不是一回事。
CDN 边缘和转码属于内容分发链路，是被监控的对象之一，不是监控系统本身的架构。
optionExplanations_en: The minimal loop is a collector fetching data, a TSDB storing the time series, and a query layer serving alerts and dashboards — drop any one piece and the whole chain breaks.
Manual patrols and email lists have no automated collection or storage — they can't keep up once scale grows, so they don't qualify as a minimal viable system.
The primary business database and marketing reports belong to the product-data stack, a different problem from operational health monitoring.
CDN edges and transcoding belong to the content-delivery pipeline — they're something monitoring watches, not the monitoring system's own architecture.

scenario: Kubernetes 集群里的服务实例会自动扩缩容，静态 scrape 列表经常漏掉新实例。
scenario_en: Service instances in a Kubernetes cluster scale up and down automatically, so a static scrape list often misses new instances.
q: collector 前应接入什么组件？
q_en: What should the collector integrate with?
options: service discoverer
手动维护的静态 IP 清单文件
用户本地浏览器保存的书签列表
定期批处理运行的离线账单系统
options_en: A service discoverer.
A manually maintained static IP list file.
A list of bookmarks saved in the user's local browser.
An offline billing system that runs as a periodic batch job.
why: service discoverer 从 Kubernetes、EC2 或 Consul 找到活跃端点，collector 才能自动覆盖新实例。代价是发现系统本身也要监控。
why_en: Service discovery lets the collector scrape dynamic instances as they appear and disappear.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有几台固定机器，静态列表更简单。
tradeoff: 动态覆盖能力 vs 发现系统依赖

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络层地址和转发协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP is the network-layer addressing and forwarding protocol.

optionExplanations: 实例随集群自动扩缩容时，接一个能查 EC2 或 Consul 的组件，让 collector 动态拿到当前活跃端点，新实例上线就自动被纳入抓取。
如果只有几台固定不变的机器，手动维护的静态清单确实更简单；但这里实例会自动扩缩容，静态清单很快就会漏掉新实例。
浏览器书签是给人用的个人收藏，跟 collector 该去哪些服务器端点抓指标毫无关系。
离线账单系统是批处理的计费流程，跟实时发现要抓取的活跃实例是完全不同的系统。
optionExplanations_en: When instances scale up and down with the cluster, wiring in a component that queries EC2 or Consul lets the collector fetch the currently active endpoints dynamically, so new instances are picked up automatically.
For a handful of fixed machines, a manually maintained static list really is simpler; but here instances autoscale, so a static list quickly misses new ones.
Browser bookmarks are a personal collection for humans — unrelated to which server endpoints the collector should scrape.
An offline billing system is a batch billing pipeline, a completely different system from discovering active instances in real time.

q: 监控采集日志时消息里至少要带什么？
q_en: What should a monitoring log message carry at minimum?
text: 日志进入分布式消息队列时，至少带 {{service name}}、{{service id}} 和错误或事件描述，collector 才能聚合到正确来源。
text_en: When logs enter a distributed queue, they should carry {{service name}}, {{service id}}, and an error or event description.
why: 没有服务名和实例标识，后面只能看到一堆匿名错误。队列的作用是解耦生产者和 collector，吸收突发日志。
why_en: Service identity makes logs attributable, and the queue decouples producers from collectors during bursts.

scenario: 团队希望 CPU > 90% 时发 Slack，磁盘空间低时发邮件，不同规则可在线调整。
scenario_en: The team wants CPU > 90% to send Slack, low disk to send email, and rules to be editable online.
q: 告警配置应放在哪里？
q_en: Where should alert configuration live?
options: rules DB + alert manager
业务代码硬编码 + 手工发布
仪表盘标题 + 值班人口头约定
用户 cookie + 浏览器本地判断
options_en: Rules DB plus alert manager.
Hard-coded business logic plus manual deploys.
Dashboard titles plus verbal on-call agreements.
User cookies plus browser-side decisions.
why: rules DB 让阈值和动作可配置，alert manager 统一执行检查和通知。代价是规则变更也要审计，避免误报风暴。
why_en: A rules database keeps alert thresholds and actions configurable while the alert manager evaluates them centrally.
whenOtherWins: 极小系统可以先把少量规则写进配置文件，但不要散在业务代码里。
tradeoff: 集中可配置性 vs 规则管理复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: 执行程序指令的处理器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CPU is the processor that executes program instructions.

optionExplanations: 想让不同规则能在线调整，就把阈值放进数据库，交给一个统一的检查执行组件负责触发和发通知。
极小系统先把少量规则写进配置文件问题不大；但硬编码进业务代码、每次改都要发版，规则一多就没法维护。
仪表盘标题和口头约定没有被系统真正执行，值班人一旦忘记或换人，规则就形同虚设。
告警是服务端该做的判断，浏览器 cookie 只在用户打开页面时才有效，没法在后台持续检测阈值。
optionExplanations_en: To let different rules be adjusted online, put the thresholds in a database and hand evaluation and notification off to one centralized checker.
For a tiny system, a handful of rules in a config file is fine; but hardcoding into business code and shipping a release for every change becomes unmanageable as rules multiply.
A dashboard title and a verbal agreement aren't actually enforced by the system — once the on-call person forgets or rotates out, the rule is effectively gone.
Alerting is a decision the server should make; a browser cookie only exists while the user has the page open, so it can't continuously check thresholds in the background.

scenario: 值班工程师要在一分钟内判断是单机问题、整排机器问题，还是整个集群异常。
scenario_en: An on-call engineer must tell within a minute whether an issue is one machine, a row, or an entire cluster.
q: dashboard 最该服务哪种动作？
q_en: What action should the dashboard support?
options: 快速定位异常范围和趋势
替代所有告警通知
永久保存所有原始日志
给用户展示营销图片
options_en: Quickly locate the scope and trend of anomalies.
Replace all alert notifications.
Store all raw logs forever.
Show marketing images to users.
why: 仪表盘的价值是把大量指标变成可扫读的范围、趋势和对比。它不能替代告警，也不该承担无限期原始存储。
why_en: A dashboard turns large metric volume into scannable scope, trends, and comparisons for operators.
optionExplanations: 值班要在一分钟内判断是单机、整排还是整个集群异常时，仪表盘把大量指标压缩成可一眼扫读的范围和趋势对比。
看仪表盘需要有人主动打开，出问题时未必第一时间有人在看，替代不了主动推送的告警通知。
永久保存全部原始日志是存储层该做的事，仪表盘只负责展示聚合后的可视化，不承担长期存储职责。
营销图片是面向终端用户的产品内容，跟值班工程师排查系统健康完全是两个受众和场景。
optionExplanations_en: When on-call has to tell within a minute whether it's one machine, a whole row, or the entire cluster acting up, a dashboard compresses a mountain of metrics into a range and trend you can scan at a glance.
Viewing a dashboard requires someone to actively open it — during an incident, nobody may be looking at that exact moment, so it can't substitute for actively pushed alerts.
Keeping all raw logs forever is a job for the storage layer; the dashboard is only responsible for presenting aggregated visuals, not long-term retention.
Marketing imagery is end-user-facing product content — a completely different audience and use case from an on-call engineer debugging system health.

scenario: 所有机器只向一个中央监控服务器上报；这个服务器宕机后，业务还在跑但没有新指标和告警。
scenario_en: All machines report to one central monitoring server; when it fails, the business keeps running but metrics and alerts stop.
q: 这个设计的主要问题是什么？
q_en: What is the main problem with this design?
options: 监控面本身成了 SPOF
业务数据库一定会丢数据
客户端 DNS 一定失败
所有指标都会自动修复
options_en: The monitoring plane itself is a SPOF.
The business database must lose data.
Client DNS must fail.
All metrics repair themselves automatically.
why: 监控系统也要有可用性设计；否则最需要告警时，告警入口先没了。常见修法是 failover、分层 collector 和多副本存储。
why_en: The monitoring system must be reliable too, otherwise the alerting path can fail exactly when it is needed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个组件失效就会让整体能力失效的单点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A SPOF is one component whose failure breaks the overall capability.

optionExplanations: 所有机器只上报给一台中央服务器，这台服务器一宕机，监控和告警就跟着一起消失——监控自己变成了单点故障。
中央监控服务器宕机不会直接导致业务数据库丢数据，业务数据的可靠性由数据库自己的复制和备份负责。
监控服务器和客户端 DNS 解析是两个独立的系统，一个宕机不会连带让另一个必然失败。
监控服务器宕机后连指标都收不到，谈不上自动修复，问题只会一直隐藏到有人发现。
optionExplanations_en: If every machine reports to one central server, that server going down takes monitoring and alerting down with it — monitoring has become a single point of failure itself.
The central monitoring server going down doesn't directly cause the business database to lose data — the database's own replication and backups are responsible for that reliability.
The monitoring server and client-side DNS resolution are separate systems; one going down doesn't necessarily take the other down with it.
With the monitoring server down, metrics aren't even being collected, so nothing is being 'auto-fixed' — the problem just stays hidden until someone notices.

scenario: 集群每秒产生大量指标；团队想看近 24 小时的秒级图，也想保留一年趋势。
scenario_en: A cluster emits many metrics per second; the team wants second-level graphs for the last 24 hours and one-year trends.
q: 长期保存应怎么设计？
q_en: How should long-term retention be designed?
options: 近热细粒度，历史降采样
所有原始点永久放内存
超过一天直接丢光历史
只留下最后一个指标快照
options_en: Keep recent data fine-grained and downsample history.
Keep every raw point forever in memory.
Delete all historical data after one day.
Keep only the latest metric snapshot.
why: 高分辨率数据适合短期排障，长期趋势不需要每个原始点。降采样能控成本，但会牺牲历史细节。
why_en: Keep recent data at high resolution for debugging and downsample older data for affordable long-term trends.
whenOtherWins: 如果法规要求保留原始审计日志，指标降采样不能替代单独的审计存储。
tradeoff: 历史细节 vs 存储成本
optionExplanations: 既要看近 24 小时秒级细节，又要留一年趋势，就让近期数据保持高分辨率，历史部分逐步降采样压缩存储。
如果有法规要求保留完整原始审计日志，降采样确实不能替代它，需要单独一份存储；但这里只是要支持趋势图，降采样已经够用。
一天后直接丢光历史，意味着完全没法画一年的趋势图，跟长期保留的目标直接矛盾。
只留最后一个快照连一天内的秒级细节都丢了，短期排障和长期趋势两个诉求全部落空。
optionExplanations_en: To see 24 hours of second-level detail while also keeping a year of trends, keep recent data at full resolution and progressively downsample the older data to shrink storage.

If regulation requires keeping the full raw audit log, downsampling really can't substitute for that and needs a separate store; but here the goal is just supporting trend charts, where downsampling is enough.
Dropping all history after one day means there's no way to draw a year-long trend chart at all — directly contradicting the long-term retention goal.
Keeping only the last snapshot loses even the second-level detail from today — neither the short-term debugging nor the long-term trend need is met.

scenario: 一个公司有多个数据中心、几十万节点，单个监控服务器无法直接抓取所有机器。
scenario_en: A company has multiple data centers and hundreds of thousands of nodes, so one monitoring server cannot scrape every machine directly.
q: 采集架构应如何扩展？
q_en: How should the collection architecture scale?
options: 本地 pull，上层 push 聚合
全节点 push 到单个全球进程
取消指标，只保留原始日志
用户浏览器抓服务器指标
options_en: Pull locally and push aggregates upward.
Have every node push to one global process.
Remove metrics and keep only raw logs.
Have user browsers scrape server metrics.
why: 我会用层级：本地监控抓本地集群，再把聚合结果推到数据中心和全球层。代价是上层看到的是摘要，排障时还要能下钻。
why_en: A hierarchy distributes scrape load locally and pushes aggregates upward, while preserving drill-down paths for debugging.
whenOtherWins: 如果节点很少，单层 collector 足够，层级会增加运维成本。
tradeoff: 采集扩展性 vs 原始细节下钻
diagram:
flowchart BT
    N1["Nodes in cluster A"] --> S1["Secondary monitor"]
    N2["Nodes in cluster B"] --> S2["Secondary monitor"]
    S1 --> P["Primary DC monitor"]
    S2 --> P
    P --> G["Global monitoring"]
optionExplanations: 几十万节点单台监控服务器抓不过来时，用分层结构——本地监控 pull 本地集群，再把聚合结果 push 到数据中心和全球层。
如果节点很少，单层直接全部 push 到一个进程确实更简单；但几十万节点会直接打垮单进程的接收能力。
取消指标只留原始日志，等于放弃了结构化查询和趋势分析能力，规模越大越需要指标而不是相反。
让用户浏览器承担抓取服务器指标的职责既不安全也不可靠，浏览器根本不该有内部服务器的访问权限。
optionExplanations_en: When a single monitoring server can't scrape hundreds of thousands of nodes, use a hierarchy — local monitors pull their local cluster, then push the aggregated results up to the data-center and global layers.
With few nodes, having everything push straight to one process really is simpler; but hundreds of thousands of nodes would overwhelm a single process's ingest capacity.
Dropping metrics and keeping only raw logs throws away structured querying and trend analysis — bigger scale needs metrics more, not less.
Having the user's browser scrape server metrics is neither secure nor reliable — a browser shouldn't have access to internal servers at all.

q: 大规模监控聚合的正确数据流是什么？
q_en: What is the correct data flow for large-scale monitoring aggregation?
steps: 数据中心 primary 接收多个 secondary 的汇总
secondary 在本地集群 pull 原始指标
global monitoring 汇总跨数据中心视图
必要时 operator 下钻到本地原始数据
why: 先本地收集，后向上聚合，最后提供全局视图和下钻。这样控制全局入口压力，同时保留排障路径。
why_en: Collect locally, aggregate upward, then provide global views with drill-down to keep ingestion scalable and debuggable.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["Raw node metrics"] --> B["Local pull"] --> C["DC aggregate"] --> D["Global view"] --> E["Drill down"]

scenario: 指标走 TSDB，但排障时工程师还要按错误文本、服务名和时间窗口搜索大量日志。
scenario_en: Metrics go to a TSDB, but engineers also need to search large logs by error text, service name, and time window.
q: 日志搜索层适合补什么？
q_en: What should be added for log search?
options: Elasticsearch 这类搜索索引
只用 TSDB 存全文日志
只把日志发到 Slack
把日志存在 DNS 记录里
options_en: A search index such as Elasticsearch.
Use only the TSDB for full-text logs.
Send logs only to Slack.
Store logs in DNS records.
why: TSDB 适合数值时间序列，全文日志需要倒排索引和字段过滤。代价是日志索引成本高，要控制采样、保留期和字段。
why_en: A TSDB fits numeric series, while log search needs indexing for text and fields.
whenOtherWins: 如果只查少量结构化指标，TSDB 查询就够，不需要日志搜索集群。
tradeoff: 全文排障能力 vs 索引成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 按时间顺序存储和查询样本数据的数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TSDB stores and queries samples ordered by time.

optionExplanations: 要按错误文本、服务名和时间窗口搜索大量日志，就需要 Elasticsearch 这类带倒排索引的搜索层，而不是数值型的 TSDB。
如果只查少量结构化指标，TSDB 本身的查询就够用，不用额外上日志搜索集群；但这里要按文本内容搜索大量日志，TSDB 做不到。
把日志发到 Slack 只适合看零星通知，海量日志刷屏根本没法按条件搜索和过滤。
DNS 记录是给域名解析用的极小结构化数据，塞不下也搜不了大量非结构化日志文本。
optionExplanations_en: Searching a huge volume of logs by error text, service name, and time window needs a search layer with an inverted index like Elasticsearch, not a numeric TSDB.

If you're only querying a handful of structured metrics, TSDB's own query capability is enough, no need for a separate log-search cluster; but here you need to search large volumes of log text by content, which TSDB can't do.
Sending logs to Slack only works for occasional notifications — a flood of logs there can't be searched or filtered by any condition.
DNS records hold tiny structured data for name resolution — they can't hold or search large volumes of unstructured log text.

scenario: 运维要在一个屏幕上看 100 万台服务器哪些不可达，并快速发现是否集中在某个机房或机架。
scenario_en: Operators need one screen for one million servers to see which are unreachable and whether failures cluster by data center or rack.
q: 哪种可视化最合适？
q_en: Which visualization fits best?
options: 按数据中心/集群/行排序的 heat map
给每一台机器单独画一条完整折线图
只发送一封汇总总数的邮件通知
用随机顺序排列的纯文本列表展示
options_en: A heat map sorted by data center, cluster, and row.
A separate full line chart drawn for every single machine.
A single email notification with just the summary total.
A plain text list displayed in random order.
why: heat map 用颜色密度把大量节点压缩成可扫读视图，排序能让物理或逻辑集中故障显形。代价是它适合概览，不替代单机细节。
why_en: A sorted heat map compresses many health states into a scannable view and makes clustered failures visible.
whenOtherWins: 如果只排查一台机器的 CPU 抖动，单机时间序列图更合适。
tradeoff: 大规模概览 vs 单节点细节
optionExplanations: 要在一个屏幕上看清一百万台机器谁不可达，按拓扑排序、用颜色深浅表达状态密度，能把它们压成一眼扫过的整体视图。
只排查单台机器的 CPU 抖动时，完整折线图确实更合适；但要同时看一百万台机器，逐台画折线图根本不可能扫读完。
只发一封总数邮件看不出问题集中在哪个机房或机架，粗粒度的总数完全掩盖了空间分布信息。
随机排列的文本列表打散了物理拓扑关系，整排或整机房的集中故障没法从中看出规律。
optionExplanations_en: To see which of a million machines are unreachable on one screen, sorting by topology and encoding state as color intensity compresses them into a view you can scan in a glance.
For debugging one machine's CPU jitter, a full line chart really is better; but scanning a million individual line charts one by one is simply impossible.
A single email with a total count can't show which data center or rack the problem is concentrated in — the coarse total hides all spatial distribution.
A randomly ordered text list scrambles the physical topology, so a concentrated outage across a whole row or data center has no visible pattern.

scenario: 健康状态只需要 1 bit 表示：1=healthy，0=unreachable；现在要展示 1,000,000 台服务器的 reachability。
scenario_en: Reachability needs only 1 bit: 1 means healthy and 0 means unreachable; the view covers 1,000,000 servers.
q: 这个估算支持哪种可视化判断？
q_en: What visualization decision does this estimate support?
options: 健康总览可用紧凑 heat map
必须给每台机器画完整曲线
只能按机器名分页查看文本
需要把原始日志永久放内存
options_en: A compact heat map can support the health overview.
Every machine must get a full line chart.
Operators can only page through text by machine name.
Raw logs must be kept forever in memory.
why: 公式是 1,000,000 bits ÷ 8 = 125,000 bytes，约 125 KB。这个量级说明大规模健康概览可以很紧凑，适合 heat map。
why_en: One million bits divided by eight is about 125 KB, which makes a large health heat map compact.

termDefinitions.meaning: 约一千字节的存储单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A KB is roughly one thousand bytes.

optionExplanations: 1 比特一台、100 万台约等于 125 KB，这个体量级说明健康总览完全能压进一张紧凑的 heat map，不需要复杂结构。
既然总数据量才 125 KB，完全没必要给每台机器单独画完整曲线，那会是远超需要的开销。
分页看文本没有利用这个数据量本来就很小、可以整体一次性可视化的优势，扫读效率反而更低。
125 KB 这个体量的健康位跟需不需要永久保存原始日志是两件事，日志留存策略不该跟着这个估算走。
optionExplanations_en: At 1 bit per machine, a million machines is only about 125 KB — that magnitude means the whole health overview fits comfortably into one compact heat map, no elaborate structure needed.
With the total data being only 125 KB, drawing a full curve for every single machine is far more overhead than the problem needs.
Paging through text ignores the fact that the data is already small enough to visualize all at once — it's actually slower to scan.
