That 125 KB of health bits is a separate question from whether raw logs need permanent retention — log retention policy shouldn't be driven by this estimate.

scenario: heat map 上红点代表多次探测后不可达，绿色代表正常。
scenario_en: In a heat map, red means unreachable after repeated checks and green means normal.
q: 为什么要按机房→集群→行排序？
q_en: Why sort by data center, cluster, and row?
options: 让成片红色暴露物理或逻辑范围故障
让颜色更随机更好看
让单台机器指标更精确
让告警条件自动消失
options_en: So blocks of red expose physical or logical failure scope.
So colors look more random.
So one-machine metrics become more precise.
So alert conditions disappear automatically.
why: 排序把拓扑相邻的节点放在一起，整排或整集群故障会变成连续色块。随机排序会把范围信息打散。
why_en: Topology-aware sorting turns clustered failures into visible blocks instead of scattered dots.
optionExplanations: 按机房集群行排序让物理位置相邻的节点在图上也相邻，整排或整集群故障就会连成一片显眼的红色。
排序的目的不是为了好看，是为了让空间上相关的故障能连成块被看见，美观只是顺带的结果。
排序改变的是节点在图上的位置，不会让单台机器上报的指标数值本身变得更精确。
排序跟告警规则是否触发完全无关，它只影响可视化布局，不会让任何告警条件消失。
optionExplanations_en: Sorting by data center, cluster, and row keeps physically adjacent nodes visually adjacent too, so an outage across a whole row or cluster forms one obvious red block.
The point of sorting isn't aesthetics — it's making spatially related failures visible as a block; looking nicer is just a side effect.
Sorting changes where a node sits on the chart, not the actual precision of the metric value that node reports.
Sorting has nothing to do with whether alert rules fire — it only affects visual layout and doesn't make any alert condition disappear.

scenario: 支付系统报警后，团队需要知道是否整体错误率升高、具体错误文本是什么，以及一次请求经过了哪些服务。
scenario_en: After a payment alert, the team needs the overall error rate, the exact error text, and the services touched by one request.
q: metrics、logs、traces 分别回答什么？
q_en: What do metrics, logs, and traces each answer?
options: metrics 看趋势，logs 看事件，traces 看路径
metrics 存图片，logs 存数字，traces 发告警
三者都只回答同一个问题
traces 出现后就不再需要日志
options_en: Metrics show trends, logs show events, and traces show paths.
Metrics store images, logs store numbers, and traces send alerts.
All three answer exactly the same question.
Once traces exist, logs are no longer needed.
why: 我会用 metrics 判断范围和趋势，用 logs 看错误上下文，用 traces 串起跨服务路径。三者互补，不是互相替代。
why_en: Metrics show scope and trends, logs provide event context, and traces connect the path of one request across services.
tradeoff: 聚合趋势 vs 事件细节 vs 请求因果链
optionExplanations: 对，三者各回答不同问题：metrics 告诉你范围和趋势在不在变化，logs 给出具体事件的上下文，traces 把一次请求经过的服务串成路径。
这个说法把三者的职责完全说反了——图片、数字、告警都不是它们各自真正承担的角色。
如果三者只回答同一个问题，就不需要同时用三种工具了，正是因为它们互补才都要保留。
traces 串起的是跨服务调用路径，替代不了 logs 里具体的错误文本和上下文，两者解决的问题不重叠。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the three answer different questions: metrics tell you whether scope and trend are shifting, logs give context for a specific event, and traces string together which services one request passed through.
This flips their actual roles entirely — storing images, storing numbers, and sending alerts aren't what these three tools are really for.
If all three answered the same question, there'd be no reason to use all three — it's precisely because they're complementary that all three matter.
Traces stitch together the cross-service call path; they don't replace the specific error text and context that live in logs — the two solve non-overlapping problems.

scenario: 每台机器每秒上报 request_count，dashboard 只需要按服务和机房展示每分钟总量。
scenario_en: Each machine reports request_count every second, while the dashboard needs per-minute totals by service and data center.
q: 聚合流应怎么做？
q_en: How should the aggregation flow work?
options: 按时间窗口和标签聚合，再写入可查询存储
把每个点直接画到用户浏览器
先删除所有标签
只保存最后一台机器的值
options_en: Aggregate by time window and labels, then write queryable storage.
Draw every point directly in the user's browser.
Remove all labels first.
Store only the last machine's value.
why: 服务级 dashboard 需要按窗口和标签汇总，而不是展示所有原始点。代价是标签基数过高会让聚合和存储膨胀。
why_en: Service-level dashboards need windowed label aggregation, but high-cardinality labels can make storage and aggregation explode.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["Raw samples"] --> B["Window by 1m"] --> C["Group by service, dc"] --> D["Aggregate sum/p95"] --> E["TSDB/dashboard"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 按时间顺序存储和查询样本数据的数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TSDB stores and queries samples ordered by time.

optionExplanations: 只需要按服务和机房展示每分钟总量时，先按时间窗口和标签把原始点聚合，再写进可查询的存储供仪表盘读取。
把每个原始点都直接画进浏览器，数据量会随机器数线性膨胀，仪表盘根本渲染不过来。
标签正是用来按服务和机房区分数据的维度，先删掉标签就没法再按这些维度聚合和筛选了。
只留最后一台机器的值等于丢掉了其他所有机器的数据，总量根本算不对。
optionExplanations_en: When the dashboard only needs per-minute totals by service and data center, aggregate raw points by time window and label first, then write the result into a queryable store for the dashboard to read.
Drawing every raw point straight into the browser means the data volume scales linearly with the number of machines — the dashboard simply can't render that.
Labels are exactly the dimension used to break data down by service and data center; deleting them first means you can't aggregate or filter by those dimensions anymore.
Keeping only the last machine's value throws away every other machine's data — the total would simply be wrong.

scenario: CPU 偶尔尖峰到 91% 一秒就恢复；团队只想在持续资源压力时叫醒值班。
scenario_en: CPU briefly spikes to 91% for one second and recovers; the team only wants pages for sustained resource pressure.
q: 告警条件应如何避免噪声？
q_en: How should the alert condition avoid noise?
options: 阈值配持续时间或多次窗口判断
任何单点超过阈值立刻 P0
删除 CPU 指标
只在用户投诉后报警
options_en: Combine the threshold with duration or repeated windows.
Make any single point over threshold a P0.
Delete the CPU metric.
Alert only after user complaints.
why: 持续时间能区分短抖动和真正饱和，减少误报。代价是检测会慢一点，所以关键路径要按风险调窗口。
why_en: Adding duration separates brief spikes from sustained saturation and reduces noisy pages.
whenOtherWins: 如果是数据丢失或安全事件，单次触发也可能必须立刻报警。
tradeoff: 误报率 vs 检测速度

termDefinitions.meaning: 执行程序指令的处理器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CPU is the processor that executes program instructions.

optionExplanations: CPU 只是偶尔尖峰一秒就恢复时，把阈值配成要持续一段时间或连续多个窗口都超标才触发，能过滤掉这种短抖动。
如果是数据丢失或安全事件，单点触发就该立刻拉 P0；但这里只是普通的 CPU 尖峰，单点触发会造成大量误报。
删掉 CPU 指标只是让问题看不见，不代表资源压力真的消失了，反而失去了本该有的可见性。
等用户投诉才报警意味着故障已经实际影响到人了才被发现，比持续窗口判断慢得多，也更被动。
optionExplanations_en: When CPU only spikes for a second and recovers, requiring the threshold to hold for a duration or across several consecutive windows before firing filters out that kind of brief jitter.
For data loss or a security incident, a single trigger firing P0 immediately is warranted; but this is an ordinary CPU spike, where single-trigger firing would cause a flood of false alarms.
Deleting the CPU metric just makes the problem invisible — it doesn't mean the resource pressure is actually gone, and it loses visibility that should exist.
Waiting for a user complaint means the outage has already affected real people before anyone notices — far slower and more reactive than a sustained-window check.

scenario: 用户因为 DNS 或 ISP 路由问题完全连不到服务，服务端日志没有任何对应请求。
scenario_en: Users cannot reach the service because of DNS or ISP routing problems, and server logs have no matching requests.
q: 为什么需要客户端侧监控？
q_en: Why is client-side monitoring needed?
options: 服务端看不到请求到达前的失败
服务端日志一定能覆盖所有网络问题
客户端侧监控只用于 UI 美化
DNS 失败会自动写进数据库
options_en: The server cannot see failures that happen before the request arrives.
Server logs cover every network problem.
Client-side monitoring is only for UI styling.
DNS failures automatically write to the database.
why: 如果请求没到服务端，后端指标只会显示沉默。客户端侧或外部探测能补上可达性视角。
why_en: When a request never reaches the backend, server telemetry is silent, so client-side or external monitoring is needed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把域名解析到地址或路由答案的系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS maps domain names to addresses or routing answers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 向用户提供互联网接入的网络运营商。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ISP is a network operator that provides Internet access to users.

optionExplanations: 用户因 DNS 或 ISP 路由问题完全连不上时，请求根本没到服务端，后端日志和指标只会一片沉默，客户端侧监控才能补上这段盲区。
这正是本题想澄清的误解——请求到达前的网络问题服务端日志完全看不到，覆盖不了所有网络问题。
客户端侧监控的作用是发现真实用户遇到的连通性问题，不是给界面做美化。
DNS 解析失败发生在用户设备或递归解析器那一侧，服务端数据库根本不会自动收到这条记录。
optionExplanations_en: When a user can't connect at all due to a DNS or ISP routing issue, the request never reaches the server — backend logs and metrics stay completely silent, and only client-side monitoring fills that blind spot.
This is exactly the misconception the question is clarifying — server-side logs simply can't see network problems that happen before a request arrives, so they don't cover all network issues.
Client-side monitoring exists to surface real connectivity problems users hit — it isn't there to make the UI prettier.
A DNS resolution failure happens on the user's device or resolver side — the server's database never automatically receives a record of it.

scenario: 某个小地区用户无法访问服务，但全球总流量仍在正常日周期内波动。
scenario_en: Users in a small region cannot access the service, but global traffic still fluctuates within its normal daily pattern.
q: 只看总流量下降有什么问题？
q_en: What is wrong with relying only on total traffic dips?
options: 小范围故障会被自然波动掩盖
它能精确指出 BGP 泄漏路径
它一定没有误报
它能替代用户侧报告
options_en: Small regional failures can be hidden by normal variation.
It precisely identifies the BGP leak path.
It has no false positives.
It replaces client-side reports.
why: 总量指标太粗，局部故障可能没有显著下跌；自然流量下降也可能误报。要按地区、网络和客户端信号拆开看。
why_en: Aggregate traffic is too coarse because localized failures may be hidden by normal variation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 互联网自治系统之间交换路由的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BGP is the routing protocol used between Internet autonomous systems.

optionExplanations: 全球总流量还在正常日周期波动范围内时，一个小地区完全打不开也几乎不会让总量出现明显下跌，故障就被淹没了。
总流量是一个聚合数字，本身不携带路由路径信息，指不出问题具体发生在哪条 BGP 路径上。
总流量自然的日常波动本身就可能被误判成异常，或者掩盖真实异常，不是没有误报，是两种误判都可能发生。
总量指标看到的是聚合结果，替代不了用户侧报告能提供的具体地区、设备和错误细节。
optionExplanations_en: While global total traffic stays within its normal daily swing, a small region being completely unreachable barely moves that total, so the outage gets buried in the noise.
Total traffic is one aggregated number with no routing-path information in it — it can't point to which specific BGP path the problem is on.
Total traffic's normal daily swings can themselves be misread as an anomaly, or mask a real one — it's not immune to false positives, both kinds of misjudgment are possible.
An aggregate total shows the overall picture; it can't substitute for the region, device, and error detail that user-side reports actually provide.

scenario: 某个 AS 错误宣告大量前缀，用户流量被引到错误网络，服务商自己的机房仍显示健康。
scenario_en: An AS incorrectly announces many prefixes, user traffic is diverted through the wrong network, and the provider's data centers still look healthy.
q: BGP leak 对监控的启示是什么？
q_en: What does a BGP leak teach monitoring design?
options: 要有外部连通性监控，不能只看自家机房
只要 CPU 正常就说明用户可达
关闭所有 DNS 就能修复
所有请求都会留下 5xx
options_en: Use external connectivity monitoring, not only internal data-center health.
If CPU is normal, users are reachable.
Turning off all DNS fixes it.
Every request leaves a 5xx.
why: BGP leak 发生在自家基础设施外，内部服务可能全绿但用户到不了。监控要覆盖从用户网络到服务入口的路径。
why_en: A BGP leak can break reachability outside your infrastructure, so internal health alone is not enough.

termDefinitions.meaning: 互联网自治系统之间交换路由的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BGP is the routing protocol used between Internet autonomous systems.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个统一路由策略管理下的互联网网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An AS is a network under one routing administration on the Internet.

optionExplanations: 流量被错误宣告引到别的网络时，自家机房的内部指标可以全绿，问题在网络路径上，所以必须有覆盖到用户侧的外部连通性监控。
CPU 正常只说明主机资源没问题，跟用户的流量到底有没有走对路径完全是两回事。
BGP leak 是路由层的错误宣告问题，跟 DNS 是否开启无关，关掉 DNS 解决不了路由错误。
流量根本没到达自家服务时，连一次请求都没发生，也就不会有任何 5xx 记录留下。
optionExplanations_en: When traffic gets misdirected to another network by a bad route announcement, internal metrics at your own data center can be all green while the real problem sits in the network path — so external connectivity monitoring reaching the user side is essential.
Normal CPU only tells you host resources are fine — it says nothing about whether user traffic is actually taking the right path.
A BGP leak is a routing-layer misannouncement problem, unrelated to whether DNS is enabled — turning off DNS doesn't fix a routing error.
If traffic never reaches your service at all, no request even happens, so there's no 5xx record to leave behind.

q: 全球 prober 主动探测有哪些局限？
q_en: What are the limits of global active probers?
options: 无法经济覆盖所有 AS
合成流量不一定代表真实用户路径
能检测部分地区可达性
会自动知道每个用户浏览器错误
永远不产生成本
options_en: They cannot economically cover every AS.
Synthetic traffic may not match real user paths.
They can detect reachability from some regions.
They automatically know every browser error.
They cost nothing forever.
why: prober 有用，但它看到的是少量观测点和合成请求。真实用户分布、浏览器环境和最后一跳问题仍可能漏掉。
why_en: Probers are useful but limited because they see synthetic traffic from selected vantage points, not every real user path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个统一路由策略管理下的互联网网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An AS is a network under one routing administration on the Internet.

optionExplanations: 全球有海量自治系统，在每一个都部署探测点成本太高，实际能覆盖的只是其中一部分。
prober 发出的是合成请求，走的路径和真实用户设备、网络环境未必一致，容易漏掉真实场景才有的问题。
从有限的观测点出发，prober 确实能验证部分地区的连通性，这是它有价值的地方。
这是误解——prober 只知道自己的探测结果，看不到具体某个用户浏览器里发生了什么错误。
这也是误解——部署和运行探测节点本身要花钱，不可能永远零成本。
optionExplanations_en: There are a huge number of autonomous systems worldwide — deploying a probe in every single one is too expensive, so real coverage only reaches a subset.
A prober sends synthetic requests over a path that may not match a real user's device and network conditions, so it can miss issues that only show up in real-world scenarios.
From its limited set of vantage points, a prober can genuinely verify reachability for some regions — that's where its value lies.
This is a misconception — a prober only knows its own probe results; it has no visibility into what error happened inside a specific user's browser.
This is also a misconception — deploying and running probe nodes costs money; it's never free forever.

scenario: 服务商想接近实时知道真实用户遇到的 DNS、路由和连接失败，而不是只靠合成探测。
scenario_en: A provider wants near-real-time visibility into real users' DNS, routing, and connection failures instead of only synthetic probes.
q: 应补哪种客户端侧架构？
q_en: Which client-side architecture should be added?
options: agent + collector
用户邮件 + 人工汇总
后端日志 + 更高级别
源站数据库 + 读副本
options_en: Agent plus collector.
User emails plus manual aggregation.
Backend logs plus higher verbosity.
Origin database plus read replicas.
why: agent 能从真实客户端报告失败，collector 独立于主服务可在主路径坏时继续接收。代价是要处理采样、隐私和同意。
why_en: A client agent reports real user failures to an independent collector, but sampling, privacy, and consent must be handled.
whenOtherWins: 如果只需要粗略外部可达性，少量 prober 更简单。
tradeoff: 真实用户覆盖 vs 客户端隐私和上报成本
optionExplanations: 要接近实时知道真实用户遇到的 DNS 或连接失败，就需要客户端 agent 上报，加一个独立于主服务的 collector 接收。
如果只需要粗略的外部可达性判断，少量 prober 已经够简单了；但这里要的是真实用户遇到的具体失败，邮件人工汇总太慢也覆盖不全。
后端日志只能看到请求到达之后的情况，看不到用户设备到服务之间到底哪里断了。
源站数据库和读副本解决的是数据存储和读扩展问题，跟怎么采集客户端侧失败报告没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: To know in near real time what DNS or connection failures real users are hitting, you need client-side agents reporting in, plus a collector that's independent of the main service to receive them.
For a rough sense of external reachability, a handful of probers is simpler already; but here the goal is the specific failures real users hit, and manual email roundups are too slow and incomplete.
Backend logs can only show what happens after a request arrives — they can't reveal where exactly the path broke between the user's device and the service.
An origin database and read replica solve data storage and read-scaling problems, unrelated to how client-side failure reports get collected.

scenario: 主服务因为某 CDN 或域名故障不可达，但客户端错误报告还要送到监控后端。
scenario_en: The main service is unreachable because of a CDN or domain failure, but client error reports still need to reach monitoring.
q: collector 应如何部署？
q_en: How should collectors be deployed?
options: 不同 IP/域名/AS/CDN 失败域
和主服务同域同 CDN 同入口
只部署在用户本机本地缓存
只写入主服务数据库路径
options_en: A different IP, domain, AS, or CDN failure domain.
The same domain, CDN, and entry point as the main service.
Only local buffering on the user's machine.
Only the main service database path.
why: collector 要离开主故障的 blast radius，否则主服务坏时报告也送不出去。代价是多一套入口要运维和保护。
why_en: Collectors must sit outside the main service's blast radius so reports can still arrive during reachability failures.
whenOtherWins: 如果只收应用内业务错误，同域 collector 可能更简单，但不适合可达性故障。
tradeoff: 故障隔离 vs 额外入口运维

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络层地址和转发协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP is the network-layer addressing and forwarding protocol.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个统一路由策略管理下的互联网网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An AS is a network under one routing administration on the Internet.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把内容缓存在多个边缘位置的分发网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content at edge locations close to users.

optionExplanations: 主服务本身可能因某个 CDN 或域名故障不可达，collector 要部署在不同的 IP、域名、AS 或 CDN 失败域，才能在主服务坏时还收得到报告。
如果只收应用内部业务错误，跟主服务共用同域同 CDN 确实更省事；但这里要收的是主服务本身不可达时的报告，共用入口会跟着一起挂掉。
只部署在用户本机意味着报告出不了本机，服务商这边根本收不到任何数据。
写进主服务数据库路径意味着 collector 依赖的正是可能已经不可达的那条主路径，起不到隔离作用。
optionExplanations_en: The main service itself might be unreachable due to a CDN or domain failure, so the collector needs a different IP, domain, AS, or CDN failure domain to still receive reports when the main service is down.

For collecting purely in-app business errors, sharing the same domain and CDN as the main service is indeed simpler; but here the goal is capturing reports when the main service itself is unreachable, and a shared entry point would go down together with it.
Deploying only on the user's own machine means reports never leave that machine — the operator never actually receives any data.
Writing into the main service's database path means the collector depends on exactly the main path that might already be down — it provides no isolation at all.

scenario: 服务想让已同意的客户端知道是否启用错误报告，以及报告发到哪个 collector。
scenario_en: A service wants consented clients to know whether error reporting is enabled and which collector endpoint to use.
q: 自定义 HTTP header 可以表达什么？
q_en: What can a custom HTTP header express?
options: 报告策略和 collector endpoint
用户跨多次访问留下的完整地理轨迹和精确位置
服务端数据库账号密码和连接字符串配置
浏览器持有的私钥和本地证书完整材料
options_en: Reporting policy and collector endpoint.
The user's complete geographic trail and precise location across multiple visits.
Server-side database credentials and connection-string configuration.
The browser's private keys and full local certificate material.
why: header 可以把策略和 endpoint 作为协议化配置发给客户端。前提是用户同意，且字段要最小化，避免把隐私数据塞进去。
why_en: A custom header can deliver reporting policy and collector endpoints, but only with consent and minimal data.

termDefinitions.meaning: Web 客户端和服务器交换请求/响应的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the request-response protocol used by web clients and servers.

optionExplanations: 已同意的客户端需要知道是否启用错误报告、报告发去哪，自定义 header 正好能把这两项当协议化配置发下去。
把用户完整地理轨迹塞进 header 是过度收集，跟要不要上报、往哪上报这个配置目的完全不匹配，也违反最小化原则。
数据库密码属于服务端内部机密，绝不该出现在发给客户端的任何 HTTP 响应头里。
私钥和证书材料是客户端本地敏感凭据，服务端 header 既不该也不能替客户端管理这些。
optionExplanations_en: A client that has already consented needs to know whether error reporting is on and where reports go — a custom header is exactly the right place to send that as protocol-level configuration.
Cramming a user's full geographic trail into a header is over-collection, unrelated to the configuration goal of deciding whether and where to report, and it violates data minimization.
A database password is server-side internal secret material and should never appear in any HTTP response header sent to a client.
Private keys and certificate material are the client's own local sensitive credentials — a server-sent header shouldn't and can't manage those on the client's behalf.

q: 客户端错误监控要避免收集哪些隐私敏感数据？
q_en: What privacy-sensitive data should client-side error monitoring avoid collecting?
options: traceroute 细节
DNS resolver 细节
可识别用户的细粒度 RTT/丢包
最小化后的失败类型
用户可随时 opt out
options_en: Traceroute details.
DNS resolver details.
Fine-grained RTT or packet loss that can identify users.
A minimized failure type.
The user can opt out anytime.
why: traceroute、resolver 和细粒度网络特征可能泄露位置或指纹。最小化失败类型和可退出机制是隐私保护手段，不是要避免的对象。
why_en: Traceroute, resolver details, and fine-grained network fingerprints can leak location or identity, so reports should be minimized.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把域名解析到地址或路由答案的系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS maps domain names to addresses or routing answers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络消息往返一次的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RTT is the time for a network message to go out and back.

optionExplanations: traceroute 会暴露用户到服务之间的完整网络路径，足以推断出大致地理位置，属于该避免收集的细节。
用户用的 DNS resolver 往往和网络环境或 ISP 强绑定，收集它会成为可用来识别用户的指纹信息。
精确到能对上具体用户的细粒度 RTT 和丢包数据，本质上是一种设备网络指纹，同样该避免。
这是误解——把失败类型收窄到最小必要集合本身就是保护隐私的做法，不是该避免的对象。
这也是误解——让用户能随时退出是隐私保护机制，不是需要避免收集的敏感数据。
optionExplanations_en: A traceroute exposes the full network path between the user and the service, which is enough to infer rough geographic location — exactly the kind of detail to avoid collecting.
The DNS resolver a user uses is often tightly tied to their network or ISP, so collecting it becomes fingerprinting information that can identify them.
Fine-grained RTT and packet-loss data precise enough to match a specific user is effectively a device and network fingerprint, and should also be avoided.
This is a misconception — narrowing failure types down to the minimal necessary set is itself a privacy-protecting practice, not something to avoid.
This is also a misconception — letting users opt out at any time is a privacy safeguard, not sensitive data that needs to be avoided.

scenario: 用户最后一公里完全断网，agent 发现错误但 collector 也无法连接。
scenario_en: The user's last-mile Internet is down; the agent observes errors but cannot reach the collector.
q: agent 应如何处理这类报告？
q_en: How should the agent handle these reports?
options: 本地有限缓冲，恢复网络后再上报
无限写满用户磁盘
阻塞用户所有操作直到上报成功
丢掉同意设置直接探测
options_en: Buffer a bounded amount locally and report after connectivity returns.
Write unbounded data until the user's disk is full.
Block all user actions until reporting succeeds.
Ignore consent and probe directly.
why: 最后一公里故障下实时上报不可能，只能有限 store-and-forward。代价是上报延迟，且本地缓冲要有大小和隐私控制。
why_en: For last-mile outages, bounded store-and-forward is the practical option, with delayed reporting and local privacy controls.
optionExplanations: 最后一公里完全断网时，agent 只能先把报告存进有限大小的本地缓冲，等网络恢复后再补发上去。
无限制地写满用户磁盘会挤占用户自己的存储空间，跟有限缓冲这个约束正好相反。
阻塞用户所有操作等着上报成功，会让一次监控上报变成影响用户正常使用的故障，代价太大了。
丢掉同意设置直接探测违反了用户此前设定的隐私授权，不能因为网络断了就绕过同意机制。
optionExplanations_en: When the last mile is completely down, the agent can only buffer the report locally in a bounded amount of storage and re-send once the network comes back.
Writing to the user's disk without any bound crowds out their own storage space — the opposite of the bounded-buffer constraint that's actually needed.
Blocking every user action until the report successfully sends turns a monitoring upload into something that breaks the user's normal experience — far too costly.
Dropping the consent setting and probing anyway violates the privacy authorization the user already gave — a network outage doesn't justify bypassing consent.

scenario: 客户端错误事件量巨大，全部上报会让 collector 和隐私审查成本都过高。
scenario_en: Client-side error volume is huge, and reporting every event would be too expensive for collectors and privacy review.
q: 应采用什么成本控制手段？
q_en: What cost-control technique should be used?
options: 按用户或事件采样，例如 1%
收集每个用户的完整网络路径
关闭所有 consent
让主服务同步等待报告写入
options_en: Sample users or events, for example 1%.
Collect every user's full network path.
Disable all consent.
Make the main service synchronously wait for report writes.
why: 采样能保留趋势信号，同时把上报量和隐私暴露面降下来。代价是小规模故障可能需要分层采样或提高特定区域采样率。
why_en: Sampling preserves trend signals while reducing ingestion cost and privacy exposure.
whenOtherWins: 如果是安全事件或极小用户群故障，可能需要临时提高采样率。
tradeoff: 成本和隐私暴露 vs 小样本可见性
optionExplanations: 事件量巨大、全量上报成本和隐私审查都吃不消时，按用户或事件抽一小部分（比如 1%）仍能看出大致走向，还能把上报量和暴露面一起压下来。
如果是安全事件或影响面极小的用户群故障，确实可能需要临时提高甚至收集完整路径；但常态下全量收集完整网络路径成本和隐私风险都太高。
关闭所有同意机制不是降成本手段，而是直接违反了用户此前的隐私授权，不能这么做。
让主服务同步等报告写入会把监控上报的延迟直接加到用户请求的响应时间上，拖慢了本该独立的主路径。
optionExplanations_en: When event volume is huge and full reporting is too costly both operationally and for privacy review, sampling a small slice by user or event — say 1% — still shows the overall direction while cutting both volume and exposure.

For a security incident or an outage affecting a very small user group, temporarily raising the rate or even collecting full paths can be warranted; but collecting every user's complete network path as the default is too costly and too privacy-risky.
Turning off consent entirely isn't a cost-control lever — it directly violates the privacy authorization users already gave, and it isn't an option.
Having the main service wait synchronously for the report to be written adds monitoring latency straight onto the user's request response time, slowing down a path that should stay independent.

scenario: collector 收到全球客户端错误报告后，要在几分钟内发现某地区 DNS 失败率突然升高。
scenario_en: After collectors receive global client error reports, the team must detect a regional DNS failure spike within minutes.
q: collector 后面应接什么处理方式？
q_en: What processing style should follow the collectors?
options: stream processing 做近实时聚合
每周手动下载全部 CSV 文件后再排查
只写入冷 blob 存储且完全不做在线分析
要求所有用户重新提交错误报告并等待
options_en: Stream processing for near-real-time aggregation.
Manually download all the CSV files every week before investigating.
Only write to cold blob storage with no online analysis at all.
Ask every user to resubmit their error reports and wait.
why: 近实时发现需要流式窗口聚合错误率，并按地区、网络等维度切分。代价是流处理要处理乱序、重复和背压。
why_en: Near-real-time detection needs streaming windows grouped by region and network dimensions.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是月度趋势报表，离线批处理更便宜。
tradeoff: 检测时效 vs 流处理复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: 把域名解析到地址或路由答案的系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS maps domain names to addresses or routing answers.

optionExplanations: 要在几分钟内发现某地区 DNS 失败率突然升高，就需要 stream processing 按时间窗口做近实时聚合，并按地区网络切分。
如果只是要出月度趋势报表，每周批量下载分析确实更省成本；但这里要求几分钟级发现异常，批处理的延迟根本跟不上。
只写冷存储不做在线分析，等于把数据存起来但没人实时看，压根检测不到刚发生的异常。
让用户重新提交报告既慢又麻烦，数据已经在 collector 手上了，没必要也不该要求用户重来一遍。
optionExplanations_en: Catching a spike in a region's DNS failure rate within minutes requires stream processing to aggregate over time windows in near real time, sliced by region and network.
For a monthly trend report, downloading and analyzing weekly batches really is cheaper; but here the requirement is minute-scale detection, and batch latency simply can't keep up.
Writing only to cold storage with no online analysis means the data just sits there with nobody watching it live — it can't detect an anomaly as it happens.
Asking users to resubmit their reports is slow and disruptive — the data is already in the collector's hands, so there's no need, and no reason, to make users redo it.

q: 客户端错误监控的端到端链路顺序是什么？

steps: 独立 collector 接收并做分层聚合

why_en: Policy and endpoint come first, then consented clients report, collectors aggregate, streams detect spikes, and alerts notify engineers.
